what_it_does: Each output has a range and each input has a range, and a value is mapped from one to the other as it crosses the link, with inversion by swapping the input's limits. Most connections need no scaling actor.
max_check: Max has the scale object (registry). Scaling is an object on the cord, not a property of the connection. zmap and parameter ranges not re-read this session.
notes: A design difference, not a missing function. Better in Isadora for beginners; hides the mapping from view, which Max's patch-is-the-documentation rule would dislike.
theme: Every parameter addressable: OSC, learn, binding, expressions

capability: Control Panels scoped to groups of Scenes, linked by Control ID
what_it_does: The operator interface is a separate panel whose controls reach actor inputs and outputs by ID number, not by cords. A panel belongs to a run of Scenes, so the interface on screen changes as the show moves on. Ready-made controls include a Scene list, GO and BACK buttons, a Stage thumbnail and a timecode display.
max_check: Max's presentation view is one per patcher; thispatcher setactivetab (refpage read) switches tabs. Nothing ties an interface page to a position in a show. Scene Select, Next Cue, Prev Cue have no counterpart because there are no Scenes.
theme: Scenes and cues as the structure of a show

capability: Bin Picker: clickable thumbnail grid of a media bin
what_it_does: A control that shows the files in a media bin as a grid of names or thumbnails; clicking one sends its number to any player. Media is addressed by index everywhere, so any number can pick a clip.
max_check: Read refpages: jit.playlist organizes video clips with a visual strip per clip; chooser is a scrolling list of selectable items. Neither is a thumbnail grid that feeds an arbitrary player. Only the first 650 characters of the Bin Picker entry were read.

capability: Run-only, password-locked show files with graded permissions
what_it_does: A document can be locked with a password so recipients can run it but not edit the patch. The author decides whether they may still edit the control panels, import media, or save.
max_check: Read userguide standalones_and_collectives.json headings: Max builds standalone applications and collectives. A standalone hides the patch but is a build, not a lock on an editable file with selectable permissions.

capability: Stages: numbered outputs decoupled from physical displays, saved per document
what_it_does: Patches render to a Stage number. A set-up window, saved with the document, says which displays make up each Stage, at what resolution, flipped or not. If a display is missing the Stage opens as a preview window, so the same file runs on a laptop and in the theatre. Virtual Stages are off-screen canvases at any size.
max_check: Read refpages: jit.world wraps a window, renderer and corner pin; its attribute list has fullscreen, rect, size, windowposition, enable_cornerpin, output_texture and no display-assignment table. jit.gl.node captures a sub-scene to a texture, the nearest thing to a Virtual Stage. Display assignment in Max is a window rectangle set per patch.

capability: Automatic edge blending from overlapping displays, with a wizard
what_it_does: Drag two displays of one Stage so they overlap and the overlap becomes a soft blend. Curve, gamma and knee are adjusted per edge. A wizard builds grids from 1x1 to 8x1 projectors from a resolution and an overlap. Mask actors do the same from inside a patch.
max_check: Grepped all refpages and bundled package docs for 'edgeblend' and 'keystone': no files. Userguide grep 'edge blend': none. Package library search 'blend' and 'edge': audio and geometry hits only. jit.gl.meshwarp (refpage read) has apply_mask and mask_mode attributes but no blend-between-projectors function.
notes: A shader in jit.gl.slab could do it; nothing shipped or installed does.

capability: IzzyMap: slice mapping inside every output, with every point drivable live
what_it_does: Each output actor contains a mapping editor. Regions of the source are cut out as triangles, quads, curved grids or compound masks built by adding and subtracting shapes, and placed on the surface. Slice position, opacity and individual point coordinates can be published as inputs and moved by sensors while the show runs.
max_check: Read refpages: jit.gl.meshwarp ('Video mapping tool', Jitter Tools package) deforms a texture on a 2D mesh with a mask and has meshdim, curvature, nurbs_order, mask_mode, save, read; jit.gl.cornerpin maps a texture by its four corners. Package search 'projection mapping': vs_output only. So one warped surface per object exists; a multi-slice editor with input and output views and compound masks does not.
notes: The composite-mapping KB article was fetched and not read.
theme: Mapping editor: slices, masks and warps on the output

capability: Dome and mirror warping from externally calibrated mesh files
what_it_does: Renders video through a warp mesh made by Paul Bourke's meshmapper, giving a correct image on a dome, cylinder or fisheye-mirror rig.
max_check: jit.gl.meshwarp refpage read: accepts a mesh_matrix and can read and save its own files. Whether it can load a Bourke-format mesh was not checked. Only the opening description of the Isadora actor was read.

capability: Media preloading handled by the host at every Scene change
what_it_does: Before a jump, Isadora reads which clips the next Scene will play, from where and at what speed, loads them in the background while the current Scene keeps running, and jumps only when they are ready. An actor can run the same preload early so a later cut is instant.
max_check: Refpage grep 'preload' found jit.polymovie, sfplay~, sflist~. Read jit.polymovie refpage: manages multiple jit.movie instances and preloads files for fast switching (Jitter Tools package). jit.movie has an asyncread message. Preloading exists per object; deciding what to preload from the next cue's contents does not.
theme: Scenes and cues as the structure of a show

capability: Record a Stage or camera and get the file back as playable media at once
what_it_does: An actor records a Stage or a live input to disk and, when stopped, places the new file in a chosen media slot, so the next actor can play back what was just recorded. Meant for live sampling of performers.
max_check: Read refpages: jit.record writes matrices to a movie; jit.vcr adds MSP audio; jit.gl.asyncread reads back the GL context. Recording exists. The record-then-appear-in-the-bin step is patched by hand (write, then read into jit.movie). The KB article was fetched and not read; its URL is from the enumerated index.

capability: Offline rendering by slowing the whole clock
what_it_does: A recording setting slows Isadora's internal clock to a percentage, so media and all time-based actors run slower and a heavy Scene records at full frame rate without dropped frames.
max_check: Read userguide non_realtime.json headings: it has sections for non-real-time audio and video. jit.record refpage: a realtime attribute, default off; when on, frames are written on a clock at the set frame rate rather than as each matrix arrives, which implies that with it off every arriving matrix becomes one frame. jit.world has a fixed_delta attribute (seen in its attribute list; description not read). So Max can render offline; the one-setting, whole-patch slowdown is the difference.
theme: Offline rendering of a whole show

capability: One-checkbox Syphon, Spout, NDI and Blackmagic output per Stage
what_it_does: Each Stage or display can also be published to other applications or to capture-card outputs by ticking a box in Stage Setup, or by an actor that turns it on for one Scene.
max_check: Package library: Syphon package has jit.gl.syphonserver and jit.gl.syphonclient; Spout appears only through Vsynth modules that need a separate Spout package. Registry and package search for 'ndi', 'blackmagic', 'decklink': nothing installed. NDI output is claimed on the Site page; the manual documents only NDI input.
notes: Third-party NDI and Blackmagic externals for Max may exist but are not installed here, so not verified.
theme: Sharing video with other apps and machines: NDI, Syphon, Spout

capability: Timecode as a data type, with MTC chase for movies
what_it_does: Timecode is a value type that converts itself to seconds, frames or text depending on what it is linked to, and compares correctly across frame rates. Actors read incoming MIDI Timecode, fire at a given time, and lock a movie to it by trimming speed and jumping when drift is too large.
max_check: Registry grep 'timecode', 'mtc', 'smpte', 'ltc': no names. Refpage grep 'time code' / 'MTC': only adstatus. Package library search 'timecode', 'mtc', 'ltc': nothing relevant. rtin refpage read: MIDI real-time messages (clock, start, stop), not quarter-frame timecode. transport and timepoint work in Max's own musical time.
notes: MTC quarter-frame messages could be decoded from midiin by hand. Only MTC input is documented for Isadora; no LTC.
review_notes: 2026-10-02 (Claude): no object whose name contains 'timecode / mtc' in Max 9's obj-qlookup.json. Third-party packages that are not installed on this machine were not checked.
theme: Timecode as a type, and chasing it

capability: MIDI Show Control send and receive by named fields
what_it_does: Builds and decodes MIDI Show Control messages from named fields: device ID, command format, command, cue number, cue list, cue path, and timecode for timed commands. The sender's inputs change to match the command chosen.
max_check: Registry grep 'msc', 'showcontrol': none. Package search 'show control': none. sxformat refpage read: formats system exclusive bytes from arguments. MSC is sysex, so it can be assembled by hand; no object knows the protocol.
theme: Controlling projectors, cameras and show gear

capability: PJLink projector control
what_it_does: Sends PJLink commands to a networked projector, with optional password, and outputs the projector's reply. Used to close the shutter between cues instead of projecting black.
max_check: Registry and package search 'pjlink': none. PJLink is a text protocol over TCP port 4352 (per the manual). Max's core registry has no TCP client: grep 'tcp' matched nothing, and 'net.' matched only jit.net.send and jit.net.recv, which carry matrices. sadam.tcpClient is installed (library entry read: 'Bidirectional TCP client'). max-mxj ships net.tcp.send and net.tcp.recv help files (seen by name, not read).
notes: Category is the nearest fit: projector hardware control.
theme: Controlling projectors, cameras and show gear

capability: VISCA-over-IP camera control
what_it_does: Controls pan, tilt, zoom and focus of PTZ cameras that speak VISCA over IP or Datavideo DVIP, with range presets per camera model. Public beta, tested by the vendor on two models.
max_check: Registry and package search 'visca', 'ptz': none. Would be raw bytes over UDP or TCP. Only the first 2,300 of 21,700 characters of the actor entry were read.
theme: Controlling projectors, cameras and show gear

capability: Art-Net DMX send and receive
what_it_does: Sends a DMX frame to an Art-Net node or broadcasts it, at a limited rate, and receives DMX so a lighting desk can drive the patch. Nodes on the network are listed in a menu.
max_check: Registry grep 'dmx', 'artnet', 'sacn': none. Refpage grep 'dmx': only a mention in serial. Package library: fxwdmxusbpro only (library entry read: sends DMX to an Enttec DMX USB Pro over serial). No Art-Net or sACN object is installed. udpsend refpage read: it has a rawbytes message, so Art-Net packets could be built by hand.
notes: Well-known third-party Art-Net externals exist for Max but none is installed, so none was verified.
review_notes: 2026-10-02 (Claude): no object whose name contains 'artnet' in Max 9's obj-qlookup.json. Third-party packages that are not installed on this machine were not checked.
theme: DMX, Art-Net and sACN in and out

capability: Lighting-style soft patch that crossfades with the Scenes
what_it_does: Cues send levels to logical channels. One receiver maps each logical channel to any set of output channels through an editable table, applies a grand master, and blends levels from two Scenes according to their fade progress, so a Scene crossfade is also a lighting crossfade. Output is formatted text for Art-Net, serial DMX or MIDI.
max_check: Registry has router and matrixctrl (names seen; refpages not read this session). pattrstorage refpage read: interpolates between stored presets, which is the nearest thing to a level crossfade. No object combines a patch table, a master and cue-driven mixing.
notes: Matrix Value Receive was read in full. Matrix Color Send, which samples pixel rows or columns of a video into the same channels for LED strips, was read in part; that sampling step alone is not a gap, since jit.spill ('Unroll a matrix into a list') and jit.iter exist in the registry. The soft patch with cue-driven mixing is the idea worth porting.
theme: Lighting fixtures driven from the picture or from geometry

capability: BlackTrax (RTTrP) tracking input
what_it_does: Receives RTTrP packets from a BlackTrax performer-tracking system, by unicast or multicast, and outputs position, rotation, velocity and acceleration for a named trackable.
max_check: Registry and package search 'blacktrax', 'mocap': none. Would need a binary packet parser.
notes: Niche; relevant to large venues.
theme: Stage tracking, motion capture and LIDAR

capability: Depth-camera skeleton tracking and a shared skeleton data type
what_it_does: One actor reads Kinect, Orbbec and RealSense depth cameras and outputs depth, colour, body masks and skeletons, and can record and replay depth streams. Skeletons travel as one value type that a decoder splits into named joints, a visualizer draws, a motion-capture suit also produces, and a JSON converter can feed from any other source.
max_check: Registry and package search 'kinect', 'openni', 'skeleton', 'pose', 'mediapipe', 'leap': nothing installed. cv.jit is installed and covers 2D image analysis, not depth skeletons. Only the opening of the OpenNI Tracker entry was read; the KB article URL is from the index and was not read.
notes: Third-party Kinect externals for Max exist but are not installed here. OpenNI Tracker is marked public beta with a long-run crash note.

capability: Leap Motion hand tracking
what_it_does: Reports the position and rotation of hands over a Leap Motion controller, and the angle and distance between two hands.
max_check: Registry and package search 'leap': none installed.
notes: Third-party externals may exist; not verified.
review_notes: 2026-10-02 (Claude): no object whose name contains 'leap' in Max 9's obj-qlookup.json. Third-party packages that are not installed on this machine were not checked.

capability: Declarative parser for serial and TCP streams that creates named outputs
what_it_does: A watcher holds a pattern describing an incoming message: literal text, numbers of given width, hex, character sets, raw bytes, and bitfields with byte order. Each named element in the pattern becomes an output of the actor, typed as integer, float or text.
max_check: Read refpages: serial sends and receives bytes; regexp applies PCRE to symbols and lists. Parsing a device protocol in Max is a chain (serial, zl or match, itoa, regexp, unpack) or a script. Nothing turns one pattern string into typed, named outlets, and there is no bitfield extractor found.
notes: Read in full. Would port well as a v8 object.

capability: Raw TCP client in the core toolset
what_it_does: Opens a TCP connection to an address and port by stream number, sends formatted bytes, and parses replies, for talking to projectors, media servers and other show equipment.
max_check: Core registry grep 'tcp': no names. jit.net.send refpage read: sends matrices and messages to jit.net.recv over TCP, not arbitrary bytes to a third-party device. Installed Sadam Library provides sadam.tcpClient, sadam.tcpServer, sadam.tcpSender, sadam.tcpReceiver (library entries read). max-mxj has net.tcp.send / net.tcp.recv help files (seen by name).
notes: Available through a package, Java or Node; missing only from the core objects.

capability: Zero-configuration value sharing between machines on a LAN
what_it_does: Sends a number to other copies of the program on the local network by channel, addressed by a machine number set in preferences or to all machines, using multicast so no IP addresses are entered.
max_check: udpsend refpage read: needs a host and port. The bundled max-mxj package ships help files named net.maxhole, net.multi.send and net.multi.recv (found by listing the package's help folder; the help files were not opened, so what they do is taken from their names only). No core registry name suggests multicast.
notes: Probably covered by the mxj classes; the later pass should open net.maxhole.maxhelp to confirm.

capability: IzzyCast: internet video, audio and data sessions between patches
what_it_does: A host creates a session and others join by a session number. Each participant can send video, audio and control data to the others, and each incoming stream arrives as an ordinary video stream in the patch. Built on the Zoom Video SDK, so it needs no network set-up; paid by prepaid participant-minutes.
max_check: jit.net.send refpage read: matrices to a jit.net.recv at a known host and port, no relay or NAT traversal. Installed 'AOO for Max' package is audio over network (seen in the package list; its objects were not read). Nothing found carries video between remote patches through a hosted service.
notes: A paid hosted service, not a pure software feature. The IzzyCast feature pages were fetched and not read.

capability: RTMP streaming straight from a patch
what_it_does: Streams a video and audio feed to YouTube, Twitch, Facebook Live and similar services from an actor, given a stream URL and key.
max_check: Registry and package search 'rtmp', 'stream': no streaming objects. The usual Max route is Syphon or NDI into separate streaming software. KB article URL is from the index; fetched, not read.
review_notes: 2026-10-02 (Claude): no object whose name contains 'rtmp' in Max 9's obj-qlookup.json. Third-party packages that are not installed on this machine were not checked.

capability: Text to speech as one object
what_it_does: Speaks a block of text with the operating system's voices, with voice, rate and volume inputs, an output device choice on macOS, and a trigger when finished.
max_check: Core registry grep 'speech', 'speak', 'tts': none. Package library: upshot_texttospeech ('text to speech engine'; library entry read, patch not opened).

capability: Speech to text as one object
what_it_does: Converts spoken audio into text inside the patch, for voice-controlled pieces. Added in an Isadora 4 point release.
max_check: Registry and package search 'speech to text', 'stt', 'whisper': none.
notes: Seen only as a heading and one sentence in the release notes; it is not in the v4.0 manual. How it works was not read.
review_notes: 2026-10-02 (Claude): no object whose name contains 'speech' in Max 9's obj-qlookup.json. Third-party packages that are not installed on this machine were not checked.

capability: Subtitle playback from SRT files
what_it_does: Given a timecode position, normally a movie's, outputs the caption text from an SRT file for that moment, ready to draw over the video.
max_check: Registry and package search 'subtitle', 'srt': none. Would be a short script plus jit.gl.text.

capability: Embedded Python with virtual environments and pip packages
what_it_does: Runs Python scripts inside the patch in one long-lived interpreter, with inputs and outputs as script values, virtual environments, pip packages, and a per-show environment folder that travels with the file. Not sandboxed.
max_check: Registry grep 'python' and 'py': no Python object. Package library search 'python': none installed. Max's scripting hosts are JavaScript (v8, js), Node (node.script) and Java (mxj).
notes: Only the first tenth of the 38,000-character manual entry was read. Third-party Python externals for Max exist but are not installed here.
review_notes: 2026-10-02 (Claude): no object whose name contains 'python' in Max 9's obj-qlookup.json. Third-party packages that are not installed on this machine were not checked.

capability: Paste-in ShaderToy shaders with automatic inputs
what_it_does: A fragment shader is typed or pasted into the actor's editor and compiled on the spot. The compiler recognises ShaderToy code, so most shaders from that site run unchanged, and time and mouse inputs appear on the actor when the shader uses them.
max_check: Read refpages: jit.gl.slab processes textures with fragment shaders and exposes shader params (getparamlist, param); jit.gl.pass runs post-processing passes from a JXP file. Max shaders live in a .jxs XML wrapper that declares params and binds; grep of the Max install docs for 'shadertoy' found nothing. So the capability is there and deeper; the paste-and-run path is not.
notes: Only the first sixth of the KB tutorial was read. JitLygia is installed and may ease shader work; not checked.

capability: Triggers by wall-clock time and date
what_it_does: Fires at a given time every day, once at a given date and time, or periodically by the wall clock. For installations that open and close on a schedule.
max_check: date refpage read: reports current date and time when asked, so a schedule is a polling loop plus comparison. No registry name suggests a scheduler; timepoint works on transport time, not clock time.
notes: Small but common in installations.
theme: Triggers from the clock or a calendar

capability: User Actors: embedded sub-patches that update every copy on request
what_it_does: A wrapped group of actors is stored inside the document yet keeps a shared identity. Closing its editor offers to rewrite every copy in every open document, keeping links and hand-set input values, or to split it off as a new variant. An on/off actor inside it stops its contents to save processing.
max_check: Max abstractions are files and update everywhere by nature; p subpatchers are embedded copies that never update each other. The embedded-but-synchronised middle case was not found. Based on the repo's userguide notes on abstractions and subpatchers, not re-read this session.
theme: Encapsulation: ports, arguments, on and off

capability: Keyframe timeline on any number port
what_it_does: Any number input on any op can be switched to animated and given keys on one shared timeline in the editor. Ops read and set the timeline's position, so the whole patch can be scrubbed, looped or jumped to a frame. A curve can also be an op of its own that feeds many ports.
max_check: Max object registry (interfaces/obj-qlookup.json, 1,323 names): 'timeline' and 'keyfram' match nothing. refpage names and digests (1,940 .maxref.xml files under C74): nothing for either word. userguide (C74/docs/userguide/content): 'timeline' in 0 files; 'keyframe' only inside CSS in parameter_mode.json. packages/query_packages.py search 'timeline' returns only Link objects; 'keyframe' returns one unrelated OSC object. Refpages read for the closest objects: function (breakpoint function editor), mtr (records and sequences messages), jit.anim.path (interpolates 3D transform points over time), pattrstorage (has interp and fade messages).
notes: Max has per-object curve and sequence tools but nothing found that keys an arbitrary attribute on a shared, scrubbable timeline. The cables page is short and says the timeline was just rebuilt; the detail is in videos, which were not read.

capability: Beat grid on the timeline and tap tempo
what_it_does: TimeLineBPM draws beat and bar markers on the timeline for a given BPM so keys can be lined up with music. BpmTap turns taps into a tempo and then sends beat triggers itself, with sync and nudge inputs.
max_check: Max object registry (interfaces/obj-qlookup.json, 1,323 names): 'tap' matches only tapin~/tapout~ variants; 'transport' matches transport. packages/query_packages.py search 'tap tempo': Upshot upshot_transport (controls the global transport with tap tempo) and a demo patch in Max for the Visual Arts. No timeline exists in Max to draw a beat grid on (see the first candidate).
notes: The tap-tempo half is a small convenience and is covered by an installed package. The beat grid depends on having a timeline at all.

capability: Offline render of a patch to an image sequence at a fixed frame rate
what_it_does: RenderAnim steps the patch frame by frame at a chosen frame rate for a set number of seconds or frames and saves PNGs (zipped if wanted) or a WebM file, with optional transparency and a chosen size. Because the timeline drives the animation, the result does not depend on how fast the machine renders.
max_check: refpage names and digests (1,940 .maxref.xml files under C74): jit.record (record a movie file), jit.vcr, jit.gl.asyncread. jit.record refpage: a realtime attribute, default off. jit.world refpage attribute list includes fixed_delta, and so do jit.phys.world and jit.anim.path. userguide (C74/docs/userguide/content): 'non-realtime' in 0 files.
notes: Max looks able to do this by combining a fixed time step with non-realtime recording, but the recipe was not found written down and was not tested. May not be a gap at all.
theme: Offline rendering of a whole show

capability: Pre-warming shaders and GPU uploads during loading
what_it_does: PreRender draws the patch at a series of timeline times while a loading bar shows, so shaders are compiled and assets uploaded before playback starts. DemoPrerender records the moments in a run where heavy events caused frame drops and pre-renders exactly those. LoadingStatus reports asset-loading progress to the patch.
max_check: refpage names and digests (1,940 .maxref.xml files under C74): 'loading' and 'progress' match no name or digest. No Max object was found that reports GPU or asset loading progress or pre-renders at future times.
notes: Useful for timed pieces where the first appearance of a scene stutters. A Max patch could fake it by drawing everything once behind a cover; no built-in was found.

capability: Shader effects that add to any material
what_it_does: 35 ops that sit after a material and insert their own vertex or fragment code into whatever shader is active: displacement, twist, bend, glow, colouring or discarding inside a 3D region. Several stack on one material, and they work on built-in and hand-written shaders alike, because every shader has marked insertion points.
max_check: refpage names and digests (1,940 .maxref.xml files under C74): jit.gl.material and jit.gl.pbr generate shaders that adapt to textures and lights; their attribute lists show no way to add vertex or fragment code. jit.gl.shader manages one complete shader. jit.gl.pass processes rendered passes, after the geometry stage. jit.geom.twist, jit.geom.displace, jit.geom.waves deform geometry in the Jitter Geometry package, on the geometry rather than in the material's shader.
notes: The gap is composability: in Max, adding a vertex deformation to a lit material appears to mean writing a whole shader. Whether jit.gl.material's generated shader can be exported and edited was not checked.

capability: Shadow filtering choices and per-branch cast/receive
what_it_does: A Shadow op after any material makes the meshes under it cast or receive shadows, with a choice of four filters (Default, PCF, Poisson, VSM), a sample count, shadow colour and an opacity mask that cuts holes in shadows. The docs explain each filter's cost and the fix for each common artifact.
max_check: refpage names and digests (1,940 .maxref.xml files under C74): jit.gl.light has shadows, shadowblur, shadowquality, shadowrange and shadowtexoutname attributes; jit.gl.pbr and jit.gl.material have shadow_soft, shadow_hard, shadow_radius, shadow_eps. No attribute naming a filter algorithm was seen. packages/query_packages.py search 'shadow': av-toolbox av.light.shadows and av.pbr.shadows (preset helpers).
notes: Max has shadows. What cables adds is a named choice of algorithm and the option to turn casting on and off per branch of the scene. The documentation of artifacts is also better than anything found in the Max userguide ('shadow' appears in 2 userguide files, neither about tuning).
theme: Names and scope: send, receive, variables

capability: PBR material extras: clear coat, thin-film iridescence, lightmaps, parallax-corrected reflections
what_it_does: The PBR material has a clear-coat layer, thin-film iridescence, a lightmap input, vertex colours used as AO, roughness or metalness, and built-in tonemapping. The environment light can correct reflections for a box-shaped room.
max_check: refpage names and digests (1,940 .maxref.xml files under C74): jit.gl.pbr attributes read in full (roughness, metalness, height_scale, parallax, parallax_shadowing, reflection, self_shadow, tex_gen, triplanar_blend, shadow_*); grep of the refpage for clearcoat, iridescen and lightmap found nothing. jit.gl.environment loads equirectangular EXR maps for IBL. Tonemapping exists in Max as a jit.gl.pass effect (tonemap.jxp found in the install).
notes: Max's jit.gl.pbr has things the cables one does not list, such as triplanar mapping and parallax shadowing, so this is a difference in feature set, not a clear lead.

capability: Node-level control of a loaded glTF scene
what_it_does: 24 ops address one loaded .glb scene by node name: transform or hide a node, replace its material, weight morph targets, play a skin with its own timing, read the scene's camera, pull out a node's geometry, or turn an animation into arrays of coordinates. Draco-compressed files are supported.
max_check: refpage names and digests (1,940 .maxref.xml files under C74): jit.gl.model lists glTF, FBX, Collada, OBJ and others as supported types, and has animation messages (animenable, animtime, animweight, animblendmode), node messages (nodebind, getnodenames, getbonenames) and material and texture group messages. 'morph' matches no jit refpage name or digest, and grep of the jit.gl.model refpage for 'morph' found nothing. Max object registry (interfaces/obj-qlookup.json, 1,323 names): 'gltf' matches no object name.
notes: Max loads glTF and plays skinned animation. Morph targets, and animation exported as arrays, were not found on the Max side.

capability: GPU-compressed textures (KTX2)
what_it_does: Loads a KTX2 texture file and reports which compressed formats the GPU supports. Compressed textures stay small in GPU memory.
max_check: Max object registry (interfaces/obj-qlookup.json, 1,323 names) and refpage names and digests (1,940 .maxref.xml files under C74): 'ktx' and 'dds' match nothing. The jit.gl.texture refpage was not read for compressed formats.
notes: Needs a closer look at jit.gl.texture before calling it a gap.

capability: Instancing fed by textures, with billboarding modes
what_it_does: One geometry is drawn many times on the GPU. Per-instance position, rotation, scale, colour and texture coordinates come from arrays, or from textures whose RGB is read as XYZ, so a shader or feedback texture can move the instances with no CPU step. Spherical and cylindrical billboarding are options.
max_check: refpage names and digests (1,940 .maxref.xml files under C74): jit.gl.multiple draws instances of a named GL object from position, rotate, scale, color and texture matrices. jit.gl.buffer has instanced and instance_div attributes and a texbuf attribute. jit.gl.tf does transform feedback on jit.gl.mesh. packages/query_packages.py search 'particle': the Compute package's jit.gp.* GPU particle system.
notes: Max can instance. Whether jit.gl.multiple runs on the GPU, and whether instance data can come straight from a texture, was not established from the refpages. Billboarding was not searched for.

capability: Distance-field (MSDF) text with per-character transforms
what_it_does: Text is drawn from a multi-channel signed-distance-field font atlas, so it stays sharp at any size, with border and shadow options. Arrays set the position, scale, rotation and colour of every character. The file browser converts a .ttf into the atlas.
max_check: refpage names and digests (1,940 .maxref.xml files under C74): jit.gl.text has a mode attribute with values 2d, 3d and outline. jit.gl.textmult treats a list of words as several texts controlled by matrices. userguide (C74/docs/userguide/content): 'MSDF' and 'signed distance' in 0 files. Max object registry (interfaces/obj-qlookup.json, 1,323 names): 'msdf' matches nothing.
notes: jit.gl.textmult works per word; cables works per character. The 3d and outline modes may already give sharp text in Max, so the practical gain could be small.

capability: Font outlines and SVG paths as geometry, and variable-font animation
what_it_does: A font's glyphs are read out as SVG path strings, and an SVG path becomes a filled 3D geometry or an array of points. The FontKit extension animates a variable font's axes (weight, width) separately for each glyph.
max_check: Max object registry (interfaces/obj-qlookup.json, 1,323 names): 'svg' matches no object. refpage names and digests (1,940 .maxref.xml files under C74): 'svg' matches no name or digest; 'font' matches only fontlist. packages/query_packages.py search 'svg': no matches. userguide (C74/docs/userguide/content): 'svg' appears in 9 files (filetypes.json among them), which were not read, so Max does read SVG somewhere, probably for drawing rather than as mesh data.
notes: No Max route from an SVG path or a font outline to mesh vertices was found. Variable-font axes were not found at all.
theme: Vector media: Lottie, SVG, font outlines

what_it_does: Plays a Lottie (Bodymovin) vector animation file into a texture or an HTML element, with frame, speed and play-mode control.
max_check: Max object registry (interfaces/obj-qlookup.json, 1,323 names), refpage names and digests (1,940 .maxref.xml files under C74), userguide (C74/docs/userguide/content) and packages/query_packages.py search: 'lottie' matches nothing anywhere. jweb (a Chromium page in a UI box) could host the JavaScript player, but nothing found gets a jweb page into a texture.

theme: Vector media: Lottie, SVG, font outlines

capability: HTML and CSS elements built in the patch and pinned to 3D positions
what_it_does: 94 ops make page elements from the graph, style them with CSS and listen to their events. TransformElement keeps an element at the screen position of the current 3D transform, so labels and buttons follow objects in the scene.
max_check: refpage names and digests (1,940 .maxref.xml files under C74): jweb hosts a web page in a UI box and has executejavascript; it is a separate box, not a layer over a jit.world window. jit.gl.camera has worldtoscreen and screentoworld messages, which give the position a label would need. No Max object was found that overlays UI elements on a render window.
notes: In cables this is free because the canvas is already inside a web page.

capability: An element of the page captured as an image for a texture
what_it_does: Takes an HTML element and outputs an image data URL of it, with a progress value and a finished trigger. The op page has no description.
max_check: refpage names and digests (1,940 .maxref.xml files under C74): jweb's rendermode attribute has an offscreen value that draws to the patcher window, not to a texture. jit.desktop copies a screen rectangle into a matrix, which would capture a visible jweb.
notes: The cables FAQ says a website cannot be rendered to a texture, which conflicts with this op's name. What the op really does is not documented.

capability: Self-arranging control panel over the output
what_it_does: 22 ops build a control panel that sits over the canvas: sliders, toggles, menus, colour pickers, an XY pad, groups, tabs and presets. Controls are chained from a Sidebar op and have no position settings. The panel ships with the exported patch.

Max's own answer is the presentation view, where every control is placed by hand (this repo's CLAUDE.md > Always Create a Presentation View). No Max object was found that lays out a panel of controls by itself.

theme: Control panels that build themselves or run remotely

capability: Every input is a visible, stored parameter
what_it_does: Each input port of an op also shows as a control in a side panel with its current value. The typed value is saved with the patch and comes back when a cable is removed. Ports are typed and colour-coded, and a cable can be dropped on a parameter name.
max_check: This repo's CLAUDE.md (If You Mention an Attribute, Show It; Drive a Real Attribute With attrui) describes the Max side: attributes show in the Inspector or an attrui, while values sent to inlets are not displayed or stored by the object. attrui refpage digest: 'Inspect attributes'.
notes: A design difference more than a missing object. It removes a class of 'what value is this object holding?' questions that Max answers with extra display boxes.
theme: Every parameter addressable: OSC, learn, binding, expressions

capability: Live view of activity on every cable
what_it_does: Pressing f in the editor shows, on all cables at once, how often each one is carrying triggers or data. It is used to find branches that run more often than they need to.

notes: The Max userguide page was only sampled around the matched words, not read in full.
theme: Profiling and live views of the running graph

capability: Per-op CPU profiler and a GPU statistics op

notes: No per-object CPU profile or GPU draw statistics were found for Max. The userguide search was by keyword only.
theme: Profiling and live views of the running graph

capability: Show the final compiled shader of whatever is active
what_it_does: Placed anywhere in the render tree, ShaderInfo shows the full vertex and fragment source of the shader in use at that point, including code added by effect ops, and its uniforms with their current values.

Nothing was found that prints the generated source of jit.gl.material or jit.gl.pbr.

capability: Compute shaders in the graph

capability: Export a whole patch, visuals included, as a web page
what_it_does: A patch exports as a folder of static files: the runtime, only the ops the patch uses, the patch as JSON, its assets and a sample page. It then runs on any web server, or in an iframe, with no cables account or server.

capability: Host page API: variables, named triggers, callbacks, URL parameters
what_it_does: JavaScript on the page that hosts a patch can set, read and watch the patch's variables, call named triggers with parameters, and receive calls from the patch. Starting values can be passed when the patch is created or read from the URL.

No interface was found for outside code to drive a running Max patch other than network messages.
notes: Follows from the web-export candidate. Listed separately because the API is what makes a patch usable as a component in someone else's site.
theme: Names and scope: send, receive, variables

capability: Deploy targets and scripted export
what_it_does: The export dialog pushes a patch straight to GitHub Pages or Netlify, or builds an Electron executable on the cables servers. A command-line tool and an HTTP API with a key run the same export without the editor, so it can be part of a build script.

No scripted or headless build of a Max standalone was found.

capability: Launch flags for installations: display, fullscreen, patch
what_it_does: The standalone app takes command-line flags that open a given patch, go fullscreen, fill the window with the output, and choose the display by index, by name, as 'external' or by pixel offset. Two more flags choose which GPU to use.
max_check: refpage names and digests (1,940 .maxref.xml files under C74): jit.world has fullscreen, floating, windowposition and fsmenubar attributes; jit.window displays data in a window; jit.displays sets and queries monitor attributes; standalone configures built applications. userguide (C74/docs/userguide/content): 'command line' in 0 files.
notes: Max does all of this from inside the patch. The cables way keeps the choice of display out of the patch, which suits a start-up script on an installation machine.

capability: Several people editing one patch at once
what_it_does: Several users open the same patch. One is the Pilot and makes the changes; the others see cursors, selections and the Pilot's view, follow parameter changes and the rendered output live, can ask for the pilot seat, and can chat.
max_check: userguide (C74/docs/userguide/content): 'multiplayer' in 0 files; 'collaborat' in 1 file (standalones_and_collectives.json), which says a Project is the document to use with a version control tool such as Git. refpage names and digests (1,940 .maxref.xml files under C74): 'collab' matches nothing. packages/query_packages.py search 'collab': the Collab-Hub package, which shares data between performers' patches, not the editing of one patch.
notes: One editor at a time, so closer to screen sharing with hand-over than to simultaneous editing. Useful for teaching.

capability: Versions in op names, with update prompts, and permission namespaces
what_it_does: An op's version is part of its name. Old versions keep working in old patches, are hidden from the add-op list, and the editor offers to update them. Renaming an op updates every patch that uses it. Four namespaces decide who may use and edit an op: one patch, one user, a team, or everyone.
max_check: userguide (C74/docs/userguide/content): abstractions.json, packages.json and projects.json exist; 'version control|git' in 0 files by that pattern, though the Git sentence above was found under 'collaborat'. This repo's CLAUDE.md (A Reusable Object Has One Home on the Search Path) describes Max resolving a file by name on the search path, with no version in the name. No Max mechanism was found that keeps two versions of an abstraction side by side and prompts to update.
notes: Depends on cables being a hosted service that knows every patch. Still, the naming rule alone is something a Max package could adopt.

capability: Public patches open in the editor from a link, and can be cloned
what_it_does: A public or unlisted patch opens in the full editor for anyone with the link, who can change it without saving and clone it to their own account. Every op's page links an example patch that opens the same way, and lists patches that use the op.
max_check: This repo's CLAUDE.md describes the Max ways to pass a patch on: a .maxpat file, or Max Compressed Text pasted with File > New From Clipboard, and a help file per object. Each needs Max installed on the reader's machine. No hosted, open-by-link patch viewer was found in the userguide file list.
notes: The teaching value is that a student can open a working example with one click and nothing installed.

capability: Authoring in a browser tab with nothing to install
what_it_does: The editor runs in a web browser. The docs say no licence is bought, the runtime is MIT licensed and the main features stay free; storage, upload size and exports per day have limits tied to supporter levels.
max_check: Max is a desktop application at /Applications/Max.app. No browser-hosted Max editor appears in the userguide file list. Max's licence terms were not looked up.
notes: A property of the platform, not a feature to copy. It matters when choosing a tool for a class where students cannot install software.

capability: File conversion on upload
what_it_does: Dropping a file on the editor converts it to a form the ops read: FBX to GLB, HDR to an RGBE PNG, CSV and MIDI to JSON, a point-cloud text file to JSON. The file browser can also compress a GLB, resize and recompress images, make an SDF font from a .ttf and turn an SVG into points.
max_check: refpage names and digests (1,940 .maxref.xml files under C74): jit.gl.model reads FBX and glTF directly, and jit.openexr exists, so two of the conversions are not needed in Max. refpage names and digests (1,940 .maxref.xml files under C74): 'csv' matches nothing; reading CSV into a dict or coll was not searched further. No asset-conversion step was found in Max's file handling.
notes: Half of this exists because a browser cannot read the original formats. The MIDI-to-JSON and SVG-to-points conversions are the parts with no Max counterpart found.

capability: Face, hand and body tracking from a camera
what_it_does: Google's Mediapipe models run in the patch on a webcam or video element and output a face mesh as points and as geometry, hand landmarks for each hand, and body pose landmarks and lines. Pose tracking can also output a mask texture of the person.

This repo's CLAUDE.md names cv.jit.faces as an installed object; its help file was not read here.

This repo's CLAUDE.md describes multi-user-template, which gets browser sensor data from phones into Max through node.script. In both, the patch stays on the computer and the phone is a remote.

No speech-to-text object was found.

capability: WebSocket client ops and shared state across clients
what_it_does: Two core ops open a WebSocket and send and receive JSON. The SocketCluster extension links many copies of a patch through a server by channel and topic, with a rule that one client sends at a time. The standalone build can run the SocketCluster server and an HTTP server as ops.

capability: Editable spreadsheet op that outputs rows as objects
what_it_does: A grid edited inside the op, with named columns, that outputs a flat array, an array of rows, or one object per row keyed by column name, and downloads as CSV.

This repo's CLAUDE.md lists butter_table, a jit.cellblock replacement with sorting, filtering and lookups, in John's own package.

capability: OSC input that names itself
what_it_does: Each incoming OSC address becomes a named channel with no routing step. A scope pattern keeps or drops addresses and a setting strips leading address segments. A second operator logs every message as a table row, with type tags and bundle timestamps, and can run a callback per message.
max_check: udpreceive refpage: attributes defer, outputformat (message, osc_packet, fullpacket, rawbytes) and quiet; it has no address filter, so routing is a second object. route refpage: matches the first element of a message, one outlet per argument. Userguide topic 'OpenSoundControl (OSC)': in Max 9 every parameter-mode object gets an address of the form /<patcher>/param/<name>/<attribute> through a built-in UDP server or param.osc, osc.codebox shows a packet as a dictionary, and OSCQuery can describe the patch. Package library: o.route (odot) is the current address router and OSC-route is marked deprecated.
advice: For control coming in from an app, use parameter-mode UI objects with Max's built-in OSC (or param.osc) so addresses come from parameter names and no route chain is needed. When routing by hand, put an osc.codebox beside udpreceive as the message monitor.

capability: OSC output that sends only what changed
what_it_does: Channels are sent under their own names. One toggle chooses between sending every channel on every frame and sending only the channels whose value changed. The script version sends a list of messages as one bundle, and the number format (int, float, double) is a menu.
max_check: udpsend refpage: messages host, port, maxpacketsize, maxqueuesize, FullPacket, osc_packet, rawbytes; it sends whatever message arrives. param.osc refpage: attribute auto reports parameter changes, outputmode chooses what is sent. change refpage: passes a number only when it differs from the stored one. Userguide OSC topic: a FullPacket message is transient and must not be stored in a message box or zl.reg.
advice: Put change before udpsend (or use param.osc @auto 1) so a stream of repeated values does not flood the network. Never park a FullPacket in a message box or zl.reg.

capability: A device map between controller numbers and the patch
what_it_does: A per-device table names sliders s1, s2… and buttons b1, b2… and records which MIDI message each one is. Maps ship for known controllers and users can add their own. A patch reads s1 or b3, so changing controller means editing the map and not the patch. The page says there is no auto-learn.
max_check: Userguide topic 'Mapping': MIDI and key learn straight onto parameter-mode UI objects, stored per patcher, not available in Max for Live; a Map column in MIDI Setup chooses which ports take part, and mapped objects can send their value back out. ctlin refpage: controller number and channel are typed as arguments. Userguide 'MIDI': ports get a letter abbreviation and a channel offset in MIDI Setup.
advice: Max is ahead on learn, TouchDesigner on the indirection. Use Mapping for a one-off rig. For a patch that must survive a controller swap, keep every controller number in one place (one subpatcher of ctlin objects feeding named s buses, or a dict) and never scatter ctlin arguments through the patch.

capability: 14-bit controller pairs joined into one value
what_it_does: The MIDI input log can join a coarse controller (numbers 0–31) and its fine partner (the same number plus 32) into one 14-bit value. The page states what happens when one half is missing. The event log keeps the two messages separate, with operating-system timestamps in milliseconds.
max_check: midiparse refpage: the hires attribute is 'High-resolution Pitch Bend' only. xbendin refpage: 14-bit pitch bend. ctlin refpage: no 14-bit option. No object in obj-qlookup.json is named for controller pairs. Package search for '14-bit' and '14 bit' returned only an unrelated MPE object. Not checked: Max help patches.
advice: If a controller sends high-resolution CCs, pair CC n with CC n+32 in a few lines of v8 (coarse × 128 + fine, output when the fine half arrives). A small Butter utility would save doing it per patch.

capability: Latest-source-wins merge with pickup
what_it_does: Several sources (a MIDI fader, an OSC app, the on-screen control) feed one value. Whichever changed most recently wins and the others are brought into line. A pickup option ignores a source until it crosses the current value, so a hardware fader in the wrong place does not make the value jump.
max_check: Userguide 'Mapping': MIDI and keys set a parameter directly, and an output-mapped port sends the value back to the controller. Userguide 'Connecting Parameters': param_connect is a two-way link between a UI object and a Gen, RNBO, poly~ or jit.gl.slab parameter. pattr refpage: bindto. No object named pickup or takeover in obj-qlookup.json; package searches for 'pickup' and 'soft takeover' found nothing relevant.
advice: Make the UI object the one merge point: every source sets it and it alone feeds the patch. Where a hardware fader is involved, add pickup in a few lines of v8. A butter.pickup object is worth building.
notes: Session 1's 'Expression, export and two-way binding on every parameter' covers binding in general; this entry is the merge-and-pickup behaviour only.

capability: Any object's settings as a live table
what_it_does: One operator lists another operator's parameters as rows: name, value, mode, expression, type, range, default and menu items. The table updates as the parameters change.
max_check: getattr refpage: attributes attr, listen and prefix, message getattrlist. pattrhub refpage: getstate and getattributes report every pattr object in a patcher. pattrstorage refpage: dump and getclientlist. Userguide 'Parameter Mode': the Parameters Window lists all parameters of a patcher.
advice: For a readable dump of a patch's state, send getstate to pattrhub or dump to pattrstorage and collect the result in a dict or butter_table. For one attribute of one object, use getattr with listen on instead of polling.

capability: Component inputs that state and check what they expect
what_it_does: The input operator inside a component has a label shown on hover. It can require a set number of channels and raise an error when the input does not match, and it can keep only the channels with given names.
max_check: inlet and outlet refpages: attributes comment, cool (inlet), style and tricolor; nothing that checks what arrives. Userguide 'Abstractions' and 'Subpatchers': the comment attribute becomes the hover text. print refpage: level 2 (Error) messages also reach any error object in the patcher.
advice: In an abstraction, check the input directly under the inlet (route by message type, zl.len for list length) and report a bad input with print @level 2, so it does not fail silently further down.
theme: Encapsulation: ports, arguments, on and off

capability: Component-local settings read from anywhere inside
what_it_does: A component can hold a private block of typed parameters that any operator inside it reads by a short name. The lookup climbs through parent components until it finds the name. The values are saved with the file.
max_check: pv refpage: a named value shared only within one patcher and its subpatches. value refpage: shared by every object of that name. pattr refpage: stores a value with the patcher (autorestore, initial). patcherargs refpage: outputs the arguments and @attribute pairs typed on the box.
advice: Use pv NAME for state that belongs to one abstraction and its subpatchers, and keep value or s / r for sharing that is meant to cross patchers. Add a pattr when the value must be saved.
theme: Encapsulation: ports, arguments, on and off

capability: Addresses are paths, with names scoped by default
what_it_does: Every operator has a path. A reference can be relative, can name a parent component, or can use one global shortcut. The editor draws a dashed line for each reference, and one form of lookup raises an error when the target is missing.
max_check: send and receive refpages: one name reaches every patcher window. pvar refpage: reaches a named object in the same patcher only. pattrforward refpage: sends a message to a named object, including one inside a subpatcher, abstraction or bpatcher. Userguide 'Abstractions': the #0 prefix gives a number unique to each instance.
advice: Max's default is the reverse of TouchDesigner's: a name is global unless you scope it. Inside anything loaded more than once, prefix names with #0 (or --- in a Live device). To reach one object inside a nested patcher, use pattrforward with its path instead of a global send.
theme: Names and scope: send, receive, variables

capability: Fetching data by reference with a visible link
what_it_does: A consumer names the operator it wants, with name patterns and renaming, and the editor draws a dashed line to it. A Null at the end of a chain gives consumers one stable thing to point at while the chain above it changes. Selecting an image shares the texture and does not copy it.
max_check: send and receive refpages (no visible link). Userguide 'Textures': every texture has a name and objects pass jit_gl_texture <name>. jit.gl.slab, jit.gl.node and jit.gl.camera refpages: out_name / out_names attributes name the output texture.
advice: End each chain in one named terminal (an s NAME, or a named jit.gl.texture or out_name) and have consumers attach to that name only. Max draws no line for a wireless link, so say in a comment at the receiving end where the sender is.

capability: Instancing from any data, one attribute at a time
what_it_does: One geometry object draws many copies. The count comes from the number of samples, table rows, pixels or points in a source. Each attribute (translate, rotate, scale, rotate towards a vector, colour, texture) picks its own source and its own channel or column by name. Each copy's id is available to shaders and to picking.
max_check: jit.gl.multiple refpage: draws a named target repeatedly from position_matrix, rotate_matrix, rotatexyz_matrix, scale_matrix, color_matrix and texture_matrix (attributes targetname, glparams, dimparam). jit.gl.buffer refpage: instanced passes a different value to each drawn instance of a jit.gl.mesh, instance_div groups them. jit.gl.picker refpage: reports the name of the object under the mouse, not an instance number. patching/MAX_PATCHING.md records three pitfalls with jit.gl.multiple and jit.gl.buffer.
advice: For tens to hundreds of copies use jit.gl.multiple with one matrix per attribute. For thousands use jit.gl.mesh with jit.gl.buffer @instanced 1, one buffer per inlet. Aiming copies along a vector has to be computed (jit.gen). A helper that builds these matrices from a dict or table by column name is worth building.

capability: Frame start and frame end as script hooks
what_it_does: A script operator has callbacks for the start and end of every frame, for project start, node creation, exit, play and pause, and devices being plugged in. A delayed call can be set in frames or milliseconds, at the end of the current frame, on wall-clock time, and in a named group that can be cancelled.
max_check: jit.world refpage: attribute drawbang (prerender or postrender) sets when its middle outlet sends the draw bang; fps and interval apply only when displaylink is off. delay and pipe refpages: time-value syntax, quantize, transport. deferlow refpage: puts a message at the tail of the low-priority queue. Userguide 'Scheduler and Priority'.
advice: In a Jitter patch, treat jit.world's draw bang as the frame tick. Drive per-frame work from it (drawbang chooses before or after rendering) and not from a separate metro whose phase drifts against the frames. Keep delay and pipe for clock time and deferlow for 'after this event has finished'.
review_notes: 2026-10-02 (Claude): confirmed in jit.world's refpage: fps and interval 'only have an effect if enable is 1 and displaylink is 0', and transform-defaults.json gives displaylink 1.

capability: Ramps and smoothing that run on the render frame
what_it_does: All control data is computed once per rendered frame, and time-sliced operators fill in the frames that were skipped. A ramp that feeds a picture therefore never beats against the frame rate.
max_check: line refpage: grain is the output interval, 20 ms by default, on Max's own timer. jit.line refpage: a drop-in replacement for line whose output is timed by the render context, described as removing the stutter of unsynchronised output. jit.mo.time refpage: mode delta gives the time between frames, accum gives running time. jit.world refpage: fixed_delta locks the delta for non-realtime capture.
advice: For any value that ends up on screen, use jit.line and not line, and scale per-frame motion by jit.mo.time @mode delta. Keep line and line~ for control and audio.
notes: patching/MAX_PATCHING.md ('Prefer smooth transitions…') currently names `line 0.` for Jitter/GL float parameters; jit.line looks like the better default there. Not tested in Max.

capability: Lag with separate rise and fall, overshoot and speed limits
what_it_does: One operator slows changes with different times for rising and falling, can overshoot the target, and can cap the speed and the acceleration of a value. It can treat several channels as one vector so a point moves along a straight line.
max_check: slide refpage: logarithmic smoothing with slide-up and slide-down arguments. rampsmooth~ refpage: linear ramps of a set number of samples up and down. deltaclip~ refpage: limits the change between samples, a speed limit for signals. None has overshoot, an acceleration limit or a vector mode. No lag object in obj-qlookup.json.
advice: Use slide for rise and fall smoothing of a number and deltaclip~ for a speed limit on a signal. Overshoot and acceleration limits need gen~ or v8; a butter.lag with those four settings is worth building.

capability: Smoothing a whole list at once
what_it_does: One filter smooths every channel, and with a per-sample option every element of a long channel gets its own filter. Filter shapes include Gaussian, box, spike removal and one that keeps ramps. The width is given in samples, frames or seconds.
max_check: slide refpage: one number at a time. jit.slide refpage: cell-by-cell smoothing with slide_up and slide_down. jit.fill and jit.spill refpages: list into a matrix plane and back. mc.slide~, mc.rampsmooth~ and mc.line~ are in obj-qlookup.json as multichannel versions. zl.median refpage: median of a list.
advice: To smooth a list, do not unpack it into N slide objects. Write it into a matrix (jit.fill), run jit.slide, and read it back (jit.spill), or at signal rate send it through one mc.line~ or mc.slide~. For spikes, collect a short history with zl.stream and take zl.median.
notes: The jit.fill → jit.slide → jit.spill chain is assembled from the refpages and has not been run in Max.

capability: Spring follower for any value
what_it_does: A value follows its input as if on a spring, with settings for spring constant, mass and damping. The input can be a target position or a force.
max_check: jit.anim.drive refpage: springto moves a 3D object with a mass-spring simulation (spring_stiff, spring_mass, spring_damp), for transforms only. A name search of obj-qlookup.json for 'spring' found only jit.phys objects; package search for 'spring' found nothing relevant.
advice: For a 3D object use jit.anim.drive springto. For a plain number, a mass-spring step is a few lines in gen or v8, and is worth packaging once as a Butter tool.

capability: Integrate a rate, differentiate a position
what_it_does: One operator adds up a rate over time to give a position, with reset and limits. Its partner gives the rate of change of a value. Together they let you edit speed and get position back.
max_check: accum refpage: stores a number and adds or multiplies into it. jit.mo.time refpage: mode accum outputs accumulated running time, with a speed attribute. jit.anim.drive refpage: move, turn and grow apply relative motion over time. delta~ refpage: sample-to-sample difference of a signal.
advice: Drive continuous motion from a rate that is accumulated every frame (jit.anim.drive turn, or jit.mo.time accum with speed), so changing the speed never makes the position jump. A ramp to an absolute value does jump.

capability: Thresholds with a release level and a re-trigger delay
what_it_does: Trigger operators take a trigger threshold, a separate release threshold, a re-trigger delay and a minimum trigger length as plain settings. A logic operator turns a value into on/off by bounds and offers rising edge, falling edge, toggle and radio-button behaviour from a menu.
max_check: thresh~ refpage: low (reset) and high (set) thresholds for a signal. past refpage: bangs when a number rises above a value. togedge and edge~ refpages: bangs on zero / non-zero transitions. onebang and speedlim refpages: gate or rate-limit repeated events. Package search: Digital Orchestra Toolbox dot.schmitt~ (digest: 'Detect triggers from envelope of a signal') and CNMAT 2threshattack~ (a two-threshold attack detector).
advice: For a signal use thresh~. At message rate build the two thresholds explicitly and add speedlim or onebang as the re-trigger guard. Never put a bare `>` on a noisy sensor.

capability: Envelope from an event, with shaped segments
what_it_does: A pulse starts a delay, attack, peak, decay, sustain and release envelope. Each segment has a length and a shape, and several overlapping envelopes can be added together.
max_check: function refpage: breakpoint editor with sustain points; next continues from a sustain point; mode Curve adds a curve factor per segment and its output then suits curve~. adsr~ refpage: signal envelope with legato, retrigger and triggermode. line refpage: takes the list function produces.
advice: function into line (jit.line for a picture) gives an editable envelope with sustain through the next message. Use adsr~ when the envelope must be a signal.

capability: Smooth, seedable noise as a control source
what_it_does: One operator makes a continuous irregular curve that never repeats. Settings include type (smooth, Brownian, white and others), seed, period, harmonics and roughness. It keeps running across timeline loops and can be sampled at any point of a 3D noise space.
max_check: random refpage: attributes seed, range, cycle. drunk refpage: random walk with seed and stepsize. rand~ refpage: band-limited random signal that interpolates between values at a set frequency. jit.mo.time refpage: mode function with function perlin gives a Perlin-noise value in step with the render. jit.mo.func refpage: functions line, sin, saw, tri, perlin. jit.bfg refpage: basis functions in any number of dimensions.
advice: For organic drift use jit.mo.time @mode function @function perlin (frame-synced) or rand~ into snapshot~, not random into line. Set @seed on random or drunk when a show has to repeat exactly.

capability: Noise textures made on the GPU
what_it_does: A generator makes Perlin, simplex, sparse, cell and random noise images, several of them computed on the GPU, with seed, period, harmonics and a transform of the noise space. A second input can supply the noise coordinate for each pixel.
max_check: jit.gl.bfg refpage: procedural basis functions (noise, fractal, distorted) run as GLSL shaders, with attributes basis, scale, offset, zoom, time and others. jit.bfg refpage: the same family on the CPU. jit.noise refpage: white noise matrices with a seed.
advice: Use jit.gl.bfg for noise textures and animate its own attributes, instead of jit.noise followed by blurs and scaling.

capability: A units menu beside every time value
what_it_does: Almost every time setting has a menu beside it for samples, frames or seconds, and movie and timer positions add a fraction or index unit. The same operator can therefore be set in frames for a picture and in seconds for a cue.
max_check: Userguide 'Time Value Syntax': fixed units ms, hh:mm:ss, samples and hz, and tempo-relative units ticks, bars.beats.units and note values. metro refpage: interval in that syntax, quantize, transport. translate refpage: converts between the time formats. No frames unit is listed.
advice: Max's time values are tempo-aware where TouchDesigner's are frame-aware. For anything musical write note values and use a transport. For anything counted in frames, count jit.world draw bangs, because Max has no frames unit.

capability: Curves and lookup tables as data
what_it_does: A 0-to-1 index reads an interpolated value out of any stored curve, with settings for what happens outside the range and for cyclic curves. Generators make sine, ramp, pulse and S-shaped curves as arrays. The image version remaps colours through a gradient whose keys live in a table.
max_check: function refpage: 'You can also get an interpolated y value for any x value', with domain and range attributes. scale refpage: optional exponent argument. jit.charmap refpage: 256-point input-to-output map for matrices. jit.gradient.ui refpage: an editor that outputs one-dimensional four-plane gradient matrices.
advice: For a transfer curve, send x into function and take y, instead of chaining scale and expr. For a colour remap on the GPU, sample a gradient texture (jit.gradient.ui into jit.gl.texture) inside jit.gl.pix.

capability: Easing shape as a menu choice
what_it_does: Operators that move between values offer the shape of the move as a menu: linear, ease in and out, cubic and others. The timer can ease its custom channels between segments in the same way.
max_check: line refpage: linear ramps only. curve~ refpage: exponential ramps, signal only. function refpage: per-segment curve factor in Curve mode. jit.anim.drive refpage: easefunc linear, quadratic or cubic, for 3D transforms only. Package search for 'easing' found a demo patch in Max for the Visual Arts and nothing reusable. Butter_tools/javascript/butter_ease.js exists (file listed, not read this session).
advice: Run a 0-to-1 line through an easing function (butter_ease.js, or function used as a lookup) and scale afterwards. A butter.ease object, a line with an @ease menu, is worth building.

capability: Cells addressed by row and column names
what_it_does: A table cell is read by the names in its first row and first column, in scripts and in operators alike. Rows can be selected by name, by index, by a list of values or by a condition, and tables can be merged by matching names.
max_check: coll refpage: an index or symbol maps to a list, fields inside the list are positional. dict refpage: keys with get, set, getkeys, plus pull_from_coll and push_to_coll. Userguide 'Arrays': arrays can hold dictionaries. jit.cellblock refpage: cells addressed by column and row number.
advice: Store records as a dict (or an array of dicts) so fields are read by name. coll rows with positional fields break the first time a column is inserted.
notes: Session 1's 'Tables as a dataflow type' covers the operator family; this entry is the naming habit.

capability: Name patterns that select and generate
what_it_does: One small pattern language is used everywhere a name is wanted: wildcards, character sets, number ranges with a step, and exclusion. The same brackets generate lists of names, and a replacement form reuses what a wildcard matched when renaming.
max_check: route refpage: exact matches against typed arguments. regexp refpage: PCRE matching and substitution on symbols and lists. sprintf refpage: builds a symbol from a format. No name-range syntax appears in any of them.
advice: Name families with a numeric suffix (LEVEL_1 … LEVEL_8), generate the names with sprintf from a counter, and select with regexp. When you design a reusable object that takes names, let it accept a pattern.

capability: Text handling without a symbol table
what_it_does: Text is edited with Python string expressions in any parameter or table cell, and with operators that substitute patterns or split text into cells.
max_check: obj-qlookup.json lists 40 string.* objects (replace, replaceall, regexp, split, slice, sprintf, trim, tolower, toarray and others). Userguide 'Strings': a String is UTF-8 text held outside the symbol table, and the page says the purpose-built string objects are easier and more efficient than symbols for text work.
advice: In Max 9 do text editing with string.* objects, not by juggling symbols through sprintf, regexp and zl. Move to v8 when it turns into logic.

capability: Movie position driven by an index
what_it_does: A movie has three play modes: locked to the timeline, driven by an index you supply, or free-running. The index can be in frames, seconds or a 0-to-1 fraction, or come from a timecode. A separate audio operator follows whichever movie it is pointed at.
max_check: jit.movie refpage: attributes position (0 to 1), time, rate, loop points, autostart, unique; messages frame, jump, frame_coarse, start, stop, asyncread. jit.movie~ refpage: frame_true ('slower, more accurate'), loadram, cache_size. Userguide 'Video': files are encoded for linear playback, and loadram (viddll engine) or HAP makes jumping cheaper.
advice: When several clips must stay locked together, do not start them and hope. Drive each one's frame or position from one counter on the render tick, and use HAP or loadram so seeking is cheap.
notes: Advice assembled from the refpages; not tested in Max. Session 1's 'Tunable high-rate movie playback' covers decoding and read-ahead, not play modes.

capability: Gapless clip switching with preload and crossfade
what_it_does: Ready-made player components take a file or a folder and handle the rest: preload before playing, crossfade or fade through a colour, still-image duration, what to do at the end (loop, hold, fade, play next), and Initialize / Start controls. A switch operator can blend between neighbouring inputs.
max_check: jit.polymovie refpage: manages several jit.movie instances and 'allows for fast file switching by preloading the files'; messages readfolder, appendmovie, play <index>; attribute target addresses several outputs at once; a jit.gl.polymovie form outputs textures. jit.playlist refpage: clips with selections, next, loop. jit.movie refpage: asyncread. jit.fx.tr.xfade refpage: crossfade between two textures; Jitter Tools has eight more jit.fx.tr transitions.
advice: Where a cut must be clean, play preloaded clips from jit.gl.polymovie on two targets into jit.fx.tr.xfade, instead of reading a new file into one jit.movie. A clip-player abstraction with preload, crossfade time, end behaviour and a done bang is worth building.

capability: A frame cache on the GPU for delay, freeze and loop
what_it_does: One operator stores the last N images in graphics memory. Reading it with a negative index is a delay, switching capture off is a freeze, animating the index is a loop, and it can fill itself on load. A companion reads any stored image by index.
max_check: jit.fx.tp.delay refpage: delays a texture by a number of frames, with max_delay and frame interpolation. jit.gl.textureset refpage: a set of textures written and read by index. jit.matrixset refpage: the same for matrices on the CPU.
advice: Pick by job in Max: jit.fx.tp.delay for a delay, jit.gl.textureset for a frame store read by index (and for a freeze, by no longer writing to the slot you are showing).

capability: Texture feedback as one explicit operator
what_it_does: A feedback operator names the downstream node whose last frame it should output, so a loop is drawn with ordinary wires and no cycle error. It has a reset that passes its input through, and a pulse to clear. The control-data version does the same for channels and can add the time since the last frame.
max_check: jit.fx.wake refpage: video feedback with a convolution stage; attributes fb, ff, gain, bleed. jit.fx.tp.delay refpage. No object with 'feedback' in its name is in obj-qlookup.json or the Jitter Tools list. scans/c74-forum/forum_insights.md describes a capture → matrix → gen route for trails. patching/MAX_PATCHING.md: a message feedback loop overflows the stack unless broken with delay, pipe or deferlow.
advice: Use jit.fx.wake for trails. For a custom loop, feed a jit.gl.pix its own previous output through a named jit.gl.texture, and always give the loop a reset. A small abstraction with reset and bypass, like the TouchDesigner operator, is worth building.
notes: The custom-loop wiring is not tested in Max.

capability: Size, pixel format and edge behaviour on every image operator
what_it_does: Every image operator carries the same settings for output resolution, pixel format, input filtering and what happens past the edge (hold, zero, repeat, mirror). The warp operator's page warns that an 8-bit map gives jagged results and asks for 16-bit or float.
max_check: jit.gl.slab and jit.gl.pix refpages: attributes adapt, dim, dimscale, type, rectangle, filter. jit.gl.texture refpage: adapt, dim, type, wrap, filter, mipmap, anisotropy. Userguide 'Textures': adapt copies the size and type of the input unless dim is set.
advice: Fix @dim (with @adapt 0) at the head of a chain so the working size is a decision. Give any texture that holds coordinates or data a float16 or float32 @type, for the same reason TouchDesigner's warp page gives. Set @wrap on the jit.gl.texture when a shader reads past the edge.

capability: Many layers composited in one node
what_it_does: One operator composites any number of inputs with one blend operation. A newer one gives every layer its own crop, fit, justify, transform, opacity, level and blend mode and builds a single shader for the whole stack. Inputs can be wired or named by pattern.
max_check: Userguide 'Depth Testing and Layering': layer, depth_enable, blend_enable and blend on every drawn object; jit.gl.layer turns depth testing off and blending on by default. jit.gl.node refpage: capture 1 renders its children to a texture. Jitter Tools has 27 jit.fx.co refpages, each a two-input composite. jit.gl.slab refpage: up to 32 inputs for a custom shader. jit.gl.videoplane refpage: preserve_aspect.
advice: For a stack of N layers, draw each source on a jit.gl.layer with its own @layer inside a jit.gl.node @capture 1 and take one texture out. Chaining two-input jit.fx.co objects grows with every layer. Fit and justify are done by hand.
theme: Draw order and layering stated outright
review_notes: 2026-10-02 (Claude): Max's userguide (Depth Testing and Layering) and the GL attribute refpage settle it: depth testing is per object, on by default, and overrides layer, so each layered object needs depth_enable 0. The repo's docs were corrected 2026-10-03.

capability: Draw order and correct transparency
what_it_does: Transparent objects are either sorted by a draw-priority number per object with blending turned on in the material, or rendered with an order-independent mode that peels the scene in several passes. The page explains how many passes typical scenes need and what the mode costs.
max_check: jit.world refpage: transparency 'adds objects with a colour alpha below 1 or blend_enable 1 to a transparency pass composited with the opaque objects with proper depth buffering'; depth_sort sorts objects by distance from the camera before each frame. Userguide 'Depth Testing and Layering': to use layer, turn depth testing off on the object, otherwise depth testing overrides it.
advice: Before ordering transparent 3D objects by hand, try jit.world @transparency 1 and @depth_sort 1. For flat layers turn depth testing off and use @layer.
notes: The repo holds two notes that disagree: scans/c74-forum/forum_insights.md says @depth_enable 1 on jit.world, patching/MAX_PATCHING.md says @depth_enable 0. The userguide page read here supports turning it off for layering.
theme: Draw order and layering stated outright

capability: Shader uniforms as parameter pages
what_it_does: A shader operator lists its uniforms on pages by kind: colours, vectors, arrays filled from a channel operator, matrices and compile-time constants. A button loads the uniform names from the code. Inputs arrive as ready-declared sampler arrays, and compile errors appear in an attached info table.
max_check: Userguide 'The JXS File Format': a <param> tag declares each uniform with type, default and description. jit.gl.slab refpage: param message, getparamlist, getparamdefault, file, embed, autowatch. Userguide 'Connecting Parameters': jit.gl.slab shader parameters are suppliers for param_connect, a two-way link to a UI object. No array-from-list uniform is described.
advice: Declare every uniform as a <param> with a default and a description, and control it from a UI object through param_connect instead of `param name $1` message boxes. Pass a list of values to a shader as a one-row float texture.
notes: Session 1 has 'Compute shaders as an operator'; this entry is about how uniforms are exposed.

capability: Transform hierarchy by wiring objects
what_it_does: 3D objects become parent and child by wiring one under another or by nesting. An empty object serves as a shared parent or as a look-at target. A separate operator reports the position, rotation, bearing and distance of one object relative to another.
max_check: jit.anim.node refpage: a transform that GL objects bind to, with parent-child relationships; attributes lookat, locklook, inherit_position / rotate / scale, worldpos, worldquat; messages localtoworld, worldtolocal. jit.gl.node refpage: a render group that can be captured. jit.gl.camera refpage: lookat, locklook.
advice: Max splits what TouchDesigner joins: use jit.anim.node for parent-child transforms and jit.gl.node for render grouping. For the distance between two objects, read each jit.anim.node's worldpos and compute it in expr.

capability: A checklist for a black render
