what_it_does: A short docs page walks through a black render in order: show a checker background to see whether anything draws, add a light or a constant material, render a cube map to look in every direction, check near and far planes, check the render flags at each level, check alpha.
max_check: No equivalent page among the Jitter userguide topics read (video, video_engine, textures, graphics_processing, render_passes, depth_layer_blend, jxs_file_format, geometry). jit.world refpage: erase_color, enable. jit.gl.camera refpage: near_clip, far_clip, lens_angle. patching/JITTER_JS_PATCHING.md is cited in CLAUDE.md as listing four silent black-render traps for JS matrix code.
advice: Write the same kind of ordered checklist into patching/MAX_PATCHING.md: a non-black erase_color to see whether anything draws, the context name each object draws to, enable, near and far clip, texture size, lighting.

capability: Audio analysis delivered as ready control channels
what_it_does: A ready component outputs low, mid and high levels, kick and snare detection, rhythm and spectral centroid as channels, each with an on/off switch to save time. The spectrum operator can output one sample per hertz, and any channel set can be written into a float texture.
max_check: peakamp~, average~ (bipolar, absolute or rms) and snapshot~ refpages. fft~ and pfft~ refpages. spectroscope~ refpage: a display, with no data outlet listed. jit.catch~ refpage: signal into matrices in four modes. Package search: zsa.centroid~ and pnp.centroid~ for spectral centroid, CNMAT 2threshattack~ and Data Knot dk.cvonset~ for onsets.
advice: For band levels use filters or pfft~ into average~ rms and snapshot~. For a spectrum as a texture use jit.catch~ into jit.gl.texture. An abstraction that outputs low, mid, high and onset as plain numbers would give students what the TouchDesigner component gives.

capability: Panel states as readable values
what_it_does: Every interface element carries a set of states: pressed (per mouse button), rollover, position, drag-out, focus, key. They are read as channels or through callbacks, and fast events can be queued so none are missed.
max_check: hover refpage: sends the scripting name of the object under the cursor. mousestate refpage: button state and cursor position, polled. ubutton refpage: a transparent click region with hilite and toggle. Standard UI objects output their value only.
advice: For rollover, give objects scripting names and use hover. For press, drag and hover states inside one control, write a v8ui, as the Butter tools do.

capability: Keyboard events as a filtered table
what_it_does: One operator logs every key down and key up with its modifiers as table rows, can be limited to listed keys or to named shortcuts, and can be tied to the panels that have focus. The older channel version makes one on/off channel per key.
max_check: key, keyup and modifiers refpages. Userguide 'Mapping': Key Mapping binds a key to any parameter-mode UI object, per patcher, shown with an orange outline.
advice: Use Key Mapping to bind a key straight to a control. Keep key into select chains for keys that are not controls.

capability: Start-up order you can state
what_it_does: Script operators have separate callbacks for project start, node creation, exit and a device being plugged in or removed. Several start scripts run in the alphanumeric order of their names. Stored values can be given a start-up value that overrides whatever was saved.
max_check: Userguide 'Patcher Lifecycle': objects, then cords, then parameter initial values, then pattr restore, then loadbang and loadmess, then live.thisdevice, window, patcherargs output, DSP; subpatchers before parents within a phase; closebang and freebang on closing; the page advises not to assume order and to use trigger. midiinfo refpage: autopollinput and autopolloutput report device list changes.
advice: Use one loadbang into a trigger for anything that depends on order, and rely on the documented phases only between kinds of object. For devices that come and go, midiinfo's autopoll attributes are the MIDI equivalent of a device-change callback.

capability: One control interface for every time-based component
what_it_does: A template gives any time-based component the same controls (Initialize, Start, Play, Speed, Cue, go to done) and the same output channels (ready, running, done, fraction). The page explains three ways to install it into your own component.
max_check: Refpages: jit.movie uses start, stop, rate, position; playlist~ uses a clip number, pause, resume; mtr uses play, stop, rewind, speed; jit.anim.path uses start, stop, play, rate; transport uses its own state. Each object has its own verbs.
advice: Adopt one convention for your own abstractions and Butter tools: messages init, start, play 0/1, speed and cue, and outlets for ready, running, done and fraction. A patch that mixes five players then reads the same way everywhere.
notes: Session 1's 'Timing engine with segments, states and callbacks' covers the Timer CHOP itself.
theme: Encapsulation: ports, arguments, on and off

capability: Errors collected as data
what_it_does: A node with an error shows a marker, and so does every component that contains it. A dialog lists all current errors and jumps to each one. A table operator logs errors with severity, type and source, filtered by pattern, with a callback per error.
max_check: error refpage: 'Listens for and reports Max errors as message output', for cases where the Max window is not shown. console refpage: mirrors the Max Console inside a patcher with classfilter, patcherfilter, textfilter and showonlyerrors. print refpage: level 2 posts in the Error style and reaches error objects. Userguide 'Debugging and Probing': watchpoints on cords that print, monitor or break, with stepping.
advice: In a show patch, put a console @showonlyerrors 1 (or error into a display) where the operator can see it, so a failure is not hidden in a window nobody has open. In your own abstractions report problems with print @level 2.

capability: Bypass on every node, and stopping a whole component
what_it_does: Every operator has a bypass switch that passes its first input straight through, for testing a network without rewiring. A component has a switch that stops everything inside it from computing while keeping its last outputs.
max_check: jit.gl.slab, jit.gl.pix and jit.fx refpages list a bypass attribute. mute~ refpage: turns off the signal objects in a subpatcher, and notes that pcontrol disables all objects. poly~ refpage: mute and bypass messages. Ordinary Max objects have no bypass.
advice: Use @bypass on GPU effects for a quick comparison and mute~ for audio subpatchers. Give your own abstractions a bypass message, since Max will not supply one.
theme: Encapsulation: ports, arguments, on and off

capability: Text that stays in step with an external editor
what_it_does: A text or table operator can be tied to a file: edits in an outside editor reload into the project and edits in the project write back. File settings also accept web addresses.
max_check: filewatch refpage: bangs when a named file changes. jit.gl.slab and jit.gl.shader refpages: autowatch recompiles when the file is edited. node.script refpage: watch attribute. dict and coll refpages: read and readagain.
advice: Scripts and shaders already watch their files in Max. For data files, wire filewatch into readagain on the dict, coll or text that holds them.

capability: Named converters at every boundary between kinds of data
what_it_does: Wires only join operators of one family, so every crossing is a visible operator named for it. Each has settings for layout: how channels become rows of pixels, which table rows become channels, which point attributes become channels.
max_check: Userguide 'Conversion Cheat Sheet': patches for message to audio, audio to message, signal to event and unit conversions. Refpages: jit.fill and jit.spill (list to matrix and back), jit.iter, jit.catch~ and jit.release~ (signal to matrix and back), jit.poke~, jit.buffer~, snapshot~, jit.gl.asyncread (texture read back to the CPU without blocking).
advice: The same boundaries exist in Max, they are just not enforced. Cross each one once, with one visible converter, and stay on the GPU once you are there: reading a texture back costs a frame of latency even with jit.gl.asyncread.

capability: Change callbacks with a choice of edge
what_it_does: A script is attached to a value and runs on the events you tick: off to on, while on, on to off, while off, any change. Other versions watch parameters (value, expression, mode, pulse) and whole operators (cooked, renamed, rewired, deleted).
max_check: togedge refpage: bangs for 0-to-1 and 1-to-0. change refpage: passes only a new value. edge~ refpage: the same for signals. getattr refpage: listen reports attribute changes. v8 refpage: function names answer messages.
advice: Detect the edge in boxes (togedge, change) and send only the event into v8. A script that receives every value and tests it itself is the TouchDesigner habit carried over, and in Max it runs code at control rate for nothing.

capability: A table that reports what changed
what_it_does: A callback runs when a table changes and is handed the old table, the new one and lists of the rows, columns and cells that were added, removed or changed.
max_check: dict and coll refpages list no change notification. dict.compare is in obj-qlookup.json (not read in detail). pattr refpage: a bound pattr outputs when its value changes, for single values.
advice: Send every write to a shared dict or coll through one subpatcher that also sends a `changed <key>` message, so readers know when to refresh. butter_table could report changes the same way.

capability: Recording control gestures
what_it_does: One operator records incoming channels while an Active input is on and then outputs the recording. Another shows the recent history of any channel as a scrolling graph.
max_check: mtr refpage: records and plays back messages on tracks; bindto ties a track to a UI object by scripting name with no cords; sync follows a transport; loop, speed, write and read. seq refpage: MIDI. multislider refpage: 'Displays data as either an array of sliders or a scrolling display'. capture refpage: stores values for viewing.
advice: Max is strong here: mtr @bindto records a control and plays the gesture back into it without a single cord. For a history graph, set a multislider to its scrolling display.

capability: Blending between N inputs with a fractional index
what_it_does: A fractional index selects among several inputs and blends the two nearest: 1.5 is half of input 2 and half of input 3. It exists for channels and for images. A weighted version mixes all inputs at once.
max_check: selector~ refpage: ramptime attribute for a click-free switch. matrix~ refpage: ramp attribute. jit.fx.tr.xfade and jit.xfade refpages: two inputs. pattrstorage and preset refpages: a float such as 1.5 interpolates between presets 1 and 2, and recallmulti mixes several by weight.
advice: For audio use selector~ @ramptime. For whole sets of settings Max already has the fractional index: send pattrstorage or preset a float. For N textures there is no single object, so chain two-input crossfades or write one jit.gl.pix.

capability: Draw order is the list order, so it is never undefined
what_it_does: Surfaces are drawn in the order of the list: the first row is in front, the last is at the back. Dragging a row changes the stacking, and there is no way for two surfaces to have an unknown order.
max_check: Read jit.group-gl.maxref.xml (the shared attributes of the jit.gl objects): 'layer' defaults to 0, rendering goes from low to high, and objects in the same layer have no guaranteed order. Read the userguide topic jitter/depth_layer_blend: every object starts in layer 0 so the order is indeterminate, higher layers draw on top, and layering only works when depth testing is off (@depth_enable 0); jit.gl.layer turns depth testing off and blending on by default.
advice: Give every overlapping plane its own @layer number and never leave two at 0. Use jit.gl.layer for flat video stacks, since it already has depth testing off. Note the direction: in Max the higher number is in front, the opposite of MadMapper's top-of-list.
theme: Draw order and layering stated outright
review_notes: 2026-10-02 (Claude): Max's userguide (Depth Testing and Layering) and the GL attribute refpage settle it: depth testing is per object, on by default, and overrides layer, so each layered object needs depth_enable 0. The repo's docs were corrected 2026-10-03.

capability: Levels multiply down a chain: surface, group, video master, master
what_it_does: Each surface has its own opacity. A group has one too, and the surface's value is multiplied by it. Above that sit separate masters for video, DMX, audio and laser, and one master over all of them, each multiplying what is below.
max_check: Read jit.group-gl.maxref.xml: 'color' is red green blue alpha per object, default 1 1 1 1. Read jit.gl.node's refpage: it groups child objects so they can be rendered and captured to a texture together (@capture 1); it lists no opacity of its own. Nothing in either page multiplies one object's level by a parent's.
advice: Patch the chain on purpose: each layer's alpha is its own fader times its group fader times a master, one `*` per level, with the master fader shown in the presentation. To fade a whole group at once, capture it with jit.gl.node @capture 1 and fade the one captured texture.

capability: Blend mode is a named menu on each layer, and a group keeps blending inside itself
what_it_does: Every surface has a blend mode chosen by name next to its opacity. Putting surfaces in a group keeps their blend modes and masks from affecting surfaces outside the group.
max_check: Read jit.group-gl.maxref.xml: 'blend' takes a name (add, multiply, screen, exclusion, colorblend, alphablend, coloradd, alphaadd), each equal to a 'blend_mode' pair of numbers; 'blend_enable' defaults to 0. The userguide topic jitter/depth_layer_blend says blending is off by default except on jit.gl.layer. jit.gl.node's refpage: children can be captured together to a texture.
advice: Write `@blend screen`, not `@blend_mode 4 1`, so the box says what it does, and remember `@blend_enable 1` on anything that is not a jit.gl.layer. To stop a group's blending reaching the layers under it, render the group into jit.gl.node @capture 1 and place the result as one layer.
theme: Draw order and layering stated outright

capability: Crop the source by a rectangle first, then shape the output
what_it_does: Which part of the media a surface shows is set by a rectangle drawn over the source. Where that part lands on the projector is set separately. Changing one never disturbs the other.
max_check: Read jit.fx.subtexture's refpage (bundled Jitter Tools package): it references a sub-region of a texture without copying, with 'offset' and 'dim' in pixels. Read jit.gl.cornerpin's refpage: four corner attributes place a texture in the window. Read the Butter_tools README section on jit.butter_crop: a crop rectangle drawn on the picture passing through it; its README says the cropping inside the box has not yet been tried in Max.
advice: Keep the two steps as two objects in series: a crop (jit.fx.subtexture, or jit.butter_crop to draw it) feeding a jit.gl.cornerpin or jit.gl.meshwarp. Do not try to crop by pulling the output corners.
notes: Session 1's candidate on the surface list said Max has no input-crop view; jit.fx.subtexture supplies the crop itself, without a view.

capability: Movie loop behaviour is a named choice: loop, play once and hold, ping-pong, random frames
what_it_does: A movie's inspector has transport buttons, a playback mode chosen by name, a speed in percent, and loop in and out points that limit playback to part of the file.
max_check: Read jit.movie's refpage: 'loop' is an integer whose only described value is the default 1 (start to end); 'loopreport' mentions a palindrome mode; 'looppoints', 'loopstart', 'loopend' and 'rate' cover the in and out points and the speed. Read jit.playlist's refpage: 'loop' is on or off per clip, 'selection' sets a clip's start and end, and any jit.movie attribute can be set per clip with 'setclip'. The refpage does not list what each 'loop' number means, and holding the last frame was not found in it.
advice: Do not leave a bare number box on `loop`. Put an `attrui` on it so the mode shows its own name, and label the control with the behaviour (loop, once, back and forth). For random frames, drive the `frame` message from `random`.
notes: The meaning of each jit.movie 'loop' value should be confirmed in the help file before writing labels.

capability: One plain codec rule: HAP for scrubbing and many layers, H.264 only for straight playback
what_it_does: The manual says which codec to use for what. HAP is decoded on the graphics card and suits scrubbing, reverse and many layers, but needs a fast drive. H.264 and similar are for forward playback only; if they must be scrubbed, export them with a keyframe on every frame. It also says to add up the data rates of all clips and check the drive can deliver them.
max_check: Read the userguide topics jitter/video and jitter/video_engine: both video engines play HAP natively; the video page suggests HAP, or loading the file into memory, for random access and resequencing. The bundled 'hap' package describes itself as a HAP video engine for efficient realtime playback. Max's pages give no keyframe or drive-speed advice.
advice: Same rule in Max: transcode to HAP anything that is scrubbed, reversed, retriggered or layered. If a file must stay H.264, export it all-intra. Check the drive's read speed against the sum of the clips playing at once.
theme: Draw order and layering stated outright

capability: The manual says when hardware decoding breaks audio routing
what_it_does: On macOS, hardware decoding of H.264 and HEVC sends the movie's sound to the system's default output and ignores the program's own audio settings. The manual says so and recommends leaving it off when the sound matters.
max_check: Read the userguide topic jitter/video: jit.movie plays audio directly through the video engine, not through Max; jit.movie~ brings the audio tracks into MSP, and mc.jit.movie~ gives them as multichannel audio. jit.movie~'s refpage (bundled VIDDLL package): plays a movie and routes its audio into MSP.
advice: When a movie's sound has to pass through the patch, for a level, a mute, an effect or a chosen output, use jit.movie~ and not jit.movie. With jit.movie the sound goes out of the computer without ever reaching a cord.

capability: A movie's sound level can follow its layer's opacity
what_it_does: A switch on each movie ties its audio level to the opacity of the surface it is on, so fading the picture fades the sound. The FAQ gives this as the way to fade audio between cues.
max_check: Read jit.movie's refpage: 'vol' is the movie sound volume. No attribute links it to any drawing object's colour or alpha.
advice: Send one fader to both places: the layer's alpha and the movie's `vol` (or a `live.gain~` after jit.movie~). A video crossfade that leaves the old clip's sound at full level is the usual result of forgetting this.
theme: Draw order and layering stated outright

capability: A folder of numbered stills plays as a movie, with frame rate, cache and auto scan
what_it_does: A folder of numbered images is one media item that plays like a movie. It has its own frames per second, a setting for how many frames to preload, the same loop modes as movies, and it picks up files added to the folder while running.
max_check: Read jit.gl.textureset's refpage (bundled Jitter Tools package): it keeps a set of textures for storage and resequencing, written by 'index' and read with 'outputtexture', the texture version of jit.matrixset. jit.movie's refpage has nothing about image sequences. No object that takes a folder and plays it was found; a folder-watching object was not searched for.
advice: For a short sequence, load the frames into jit.gl.textureset once and step through them with a counter at the wanted rate. For a long one, turn the stills into a HAP movie first; that is less patching and plays better.

capability: Shader drawn once at a set size, or drawn per surface at output resolution: the user chooses
what_it_does: The same shader can run two ways. As a Generator it is rendered once into a texture of a size you type in, and every surface using it shares that picture. As a Material it is rendered again on each surface, at the projector's resolution, which is sharper and costs more. Dragging a Material into the Generators list switches it.
max_check: Read jit.gl.slab's refpage: it renders a shader into a texture; 'adapt' (default 1) takes the size from the input, and 'dim' (default 256 256) is used when adapt is off; 'dimscale' scales the output. Read jit.gl.shader's refpage: it compiles a shader and binds it to an object, so it is drawn with that object's geometry. jit.gl.pix's refpage calls it essentially a jit.gl.slab whose shader comes from a Gen patcher.
advice: Make the choice on purpose. Give a shader that has no input an explicit size, `@adapt 0 @dim <w> <h>`: the refpage only defines the output size for that case, and its default is 256 x 256. Use the slab (one render, shared by every plane) for heavy shaders shown in several places, and jit.gl.shader on the plane itself when one surface must stay sharp at any size.

capability: Changing a layer's media crossfades; changing its effect cannot
what_it_does: When a cue with a fade time swaps the media on a surface, MadMapper draws the surface twice during the fade, old media and new, at changing opacity. It does not do this for effects: a different effect just switches, and the FAQ says to use two surfaces to fade between effects.
max_check: Read jit.fx.tr.xfade's refpage (bundled Jitter Tools package): a crossfade between two textures set by 'xfade', 0 to 1. The same folder holds other transitions (jit.fx.tr.dissolve, slide, gridwipe, zoomfade and more). jit.xfade's registry digest: crossfade between two matrices. jit.playlist's refpage shows no crossfade between clips.
advice: Build clip changes as A/B: two players into jit.fx.tr.xfade, a `line` on `xfade`, and load the next clip into whichever side is at zero. Fading between two effect chains works the same way in Max, which MadMapper cannot do on one surface.
theme: Draw order and layering stated outright

capability: A warp grid with masks, undo and its own save file (Max has one: jit.gl.meshwarp)
what_it_does: A surface can be given a grid of warp points. Points are added one at a time or by subdivision, each can have Bézier handles, masks can be drawn on the same surface, and by default the input mesh follows the output mesh so the picture is not stretched.
max_check: Read jit.gl.meshwarp's refpage in the bundled Jitter Tools package (it is not in the main obj-qlookup.json, which is why session 1's search for 'warp' found no object): a draggable mesh set by 'meshdim', curvature through 'nurbs_order' / 'curvature', a 'mask_mode' for drawing masks with 'invert_mask' and 'apply_mask', 'save' and 'read' of the whole state as a JSON file, undo and redo, 'layer', and 'output_texture'. It lists no free-placed points, per-point Bézier handles, linked input mesh or feathering.
advice: Reach for jit.gl.meshwarp before building a warp editor. Save its state with `save` to a JSON file beside the patch and `read` it at load: a warp is calibration for one room, so it belongs in its own file, not in the piece's presets.
notes: Corrects session 1's candidate 'Mesh warping with free points, Bézier handles and a linked input mesh', whose Max check did not find this object.
theme: Effect chains: blend, amount and mask on each stage

capability: The mapping stage is kept apart from the content and locked for the show
what_it_does: The manual's advice for anything beyond one projector: compose the content on an off-screen buffer, publish it as a loopback, and map that one source onto the projectors. Cues then change the content and never touch the projector mapping. Surfaces and outputs can be locked against accidental edits.
max_check: Read jit.world's refpage: 'output_texture' captures the scene to a texture and 'enable_cornerpin' shows an internal cornerpin. Read jit.gl.cornerpin's refpage: 'enable_mouse' and 'drawcorners' turn the handles off. jit.gl.meshwarp's refpage has 'show_ui'. The repo's own table (CLAUDE.md, Preferred Objects) already recommends a first jit.world captured to a texture and a second stage that maps it.
advice: Build two stages: everything creative renders into one texture, and a separate mapping stage places that texture. Give the mapping stage one 'calibrate' toggle that sets `enable_mouse` and `drawcorners` (or `show_ui`), off by default, so a stray click during the show cannot move a corner.

capability: Corner and warp points can be moved from the keyboard
what_it_does: Tab steps to the next corner handle. The arrow keys move the selected point by one pixel, and by ten with Shift. The manual says the mouse is too coarse for the last few pixels of an alignment.
max_check: Read jit.gl.cornerpin's refpage: corners move by mouse in the window or by setting 'upper_left', 'upper_right', 'lower_left', 'lower_right'; it lists no keyboard control. jit.gl.meshwarp's refpage lists keyboard shortcuts for undo and redo only. key's refpage: reports key presses, no inlets.
advice: Add a small nudge patch to any cornerpin: `key` picks the corner (or Tab cycles), the arrows add or subtract one pixel's worth (1 / window width) to that corner's attribute, Shift makes it ten. It is a handful of objects and saves real time in front of a projector.

capability: Each output knows its display; fullscreen is one switch for all of them
what_it_does: An output has a Destination menu naming a real display, a size that can be copied from that display, and its own Desktop Window button. One command sends every output fullscreen on its display and another brings them back. The project can be set to open fullscreen. The FAQ lists the system settings that break this: mirrored displays, and a maximised interface window on macOS.
max_check: Read jit.world's and jit.window's refpages: 'fullscreen', 'fsmenubar', 'rect', 'windowposition' / 'pos', 'size', 'border' and 'floating' are separate attributes; neither has an attribute that names a display. Read jit.displays' refpage: 'count' and 'coords <index>' report each display's rectangle, and on Mac it can mirror and unmirror. Which display a fullscreen window lands on is not stated in the refpages.
advice: Do in the patch what MadMapper does in its menu: at load, ask jit.displays for the projector display's coords, move the window there with `rect`, then set `fullscreen 1`, all from one 'show' toggle that drives every jit.world. Check for mirroring first and tell the operator if it is on.
notes: That a Max window goes fullscreen on the display it sits on is the common practice, but it was not confirmed in a refpage here.

capability: Each output has a frame delay to line up slow and fast projectors
what_it_does: Every video output has a delay, counted in frames, so a fast display can be held back to match a slower projector in the same setup.
max_check: Read jit.fx.delay's refpage (bundled Jitter Tools package): delays a texture by 'delay' frames, up to 'max_delay' (default 30), with 'interp' (default 1) blending between the current and the delayed frame.
advice: Put jit.fx.delay on the texture going to the faster display and set `@interp 0` so frames are delayed, not blended. One object per output, placed in the mapping stage.

capability: The engine's frame rate is a project setting
what_it_does: The frame rate of the whole engine is either left on Auto, following the display, or set to a fixed number in the project's preferences. The FAQ uses it to limit the rate of an NDI output.
max_check: Read jit.world's refpage: 'fps' and 'interval' only take effect when 'enable' is 1 and 'displaylink' is 0; 'displaylink' (default 1, Mac only) ties drawing to the display's refresh; 'sync' is vertical sync; 'running_fps' reports the real rate.
advice: On a Mac, `@fps` does nothing until `@displaylink 0` is also set. Decide per patch whether the display or a number sets the rate, write both attributes on the jit.world, and show `running_fps` somewhere the operator can see.
review_notes: 2026-10-02 (Claude): confirmed in jit.world's refpage: fps and interval 'only have an effect if enable is 1 and displaylink is 0', and transform-defaults.json gives displaylink 1.

capability: One master speed and one freeze act on everything that moves
what_it_does: Master Settings has a speed that scales every animated thing at once, shaders and audio included, a Freeze Engine that stops it all, and a Freeze Video Output that holds the picture while playback carries on underneath. Shaders that must ignore the speed read wall-clock time instead.
max_check: Read jit.mo.time's refpage (bundled jit.mo package): outputs accumulated time, frame delta or a function, in step with jit.world, with a 'speed' multiplier and an 'interval' in Max time format. transport's refpage: one tempo for everything tempo-relative. jit.world's 'enable' stops all rendering. Nothing found scales every animation in a patch at once.
advice: Give a patch one time source: a single jit.mo.time (or the transport) whose output every shader and animation reads, with one speed control in front of it. Then 'slow everything down' and 'freeze' are one control each instead of a hunt through the patch.
notes: How to hold the last rendered frame in Max while the scene keeps running was not looked up.

capability: Global tempo has a source menu: audio beat detection, Ableton Link, MIDI clock, manual and tap
what_it_does: One tempo drives everything tempo-aware. Its source is picked from a menu: detected from the audio input, Ableton Link, MIDI clock, or typed and tapped by hand. There is a Resync button. The FAQ notes that animations stop when the tempo is zero or its source is disconnected.
max_check: Read transport's refpage: 'tempo', and 'clocksource' with a 'getclocksources' message that lists the active sources at run time; the page does not name them. The installed Link package has link.session (start, stop and tempo of the shared session), link.beat and link.phasor~ refpages, and an extensions folder holding link.clocksource. The package library lists pnp.bpm~ as a tempo estimator. No tap-tempo object was found.
advice: Keep one `transport` as the only tempo in the patch and feed it from a single selector (a `umenu` of sources). Read `getclocksources` to see what this machine offers. Show the tempo and warn when it is 0, because everything written in note values stops with it.
notes: Settles part of session 1's open question: transport's sources are reported by getclocksources, and Link ships a clock source extension. The source names were not read, since that needs Max running.

capability: Audio analysis arrives as a few named channels: amplitude, bass, medium, treble, beat counts
what_it_does: The audio input is analysed once, on channels chosen in the preferences, and offered everywhere as named values. Any slider can be tied to one from its right-click menu.
max_check: Read the refpages: peakamp~ reports a signal's peak amplitude; fffb~ is a fixed bank of bandpass filters with one outlet per band; snapshot~ turns a signal into numbers at an interval; slide smooths a stream of values. Max has far more analysis than MadMapper, but nothing arrives pre-named.
advice: Build the analysis once, in one place: input, a three-band split, an envelope per band, then `s AMP`, `s BASS`, `s MID`, `s TREBLE`. Every visual reads those names. Analysing the same input separately beside each effect is the usual Max mistake this avoids.

capability: Two ways in for every parameter: a direct address for the raw value, a mapped Control for range, filter and curve
what_it_does: Every parameter has a fixed OSC address built from the names of things in the project, such as /surfaces/Quad-1/opacity. A value sent there is applied as it is. A Control mapped to the same parameter adds a source range, a target range, a filter and a curve. Renaming a surface changes its address.
max_check: Read the userguide topic OSC: with OSC enabled, parameter-enabled objects get addresses of the form /<patcher name>/param/<parameter name>, with /raw and /normalized under each; OSCQuery can be switched on in the preferences. Read param.osc's refpage: 'info' and 'allparams' output every parameter's details and values as OSC. Wildcards in addresses, which MadMapper accepts, are not mentioned in either.
advice: Treat patcher names and parameter names as a public interface: choose them before giving addresses to anyone, because a rename breaks every remote. Send 0 to 1 to /normalized from generic controllers and real units to /raw from show control. In a hand-built patch, give a parameter the same two entries: a plain set, and a scaled and smoothed one.

capability: Controllers get the current values sent back
what_it_does: Each MIDI input can be paired with a feedback device, and OSC has a feedback port and address. When a value changes inside MadMapper, motor faders, button lights and tablet layouts are updated to match.
max_check: Read the userguide topic mapping: if Map is enabled for a MIDI output port, every MIDI-mapped interface object sends its control change or note to that port with no midiout object. Read param.osc's refpage: 'auto' reports parameter changes as OSC, and 'set' dispatches incoming OSC to parameters without triggering output. udpsend's refpage: sends messages and OSC packets to a host and port.
advice: Turn on Map for the controller's output port in MIDI Setup; that is the whole of MIDI feedback. For a tablet, `param.osc @auto 1` into `udpsend`, and bring incoming values in through its `set` message so they are not echoed straight back.
notes: Max is level with MadMapper here; the Max feature is easy to miss because it lives in the MIDI Setup window.

capability: A preset shows when the live values no longer match what it stored
what_it_does: After a cue is recalled and then changed by hand, the changed controls are outlined, so the operator can see the cue is no longer what is on stage. One command writes the live values back into the cue, and several cues can be updated at once.
max_check: Read pattrstorage's refpage: 'getedited' reports 1 when the data of the current preset has been edited, 'getcurrent' reports the active preset, 'storeagain' stores into the last-used slot, and 'lock' protects a slot from being overwritten. Nothing marks which control changed.
advice: Poll `getedited` after any change and light one indicator beside the preset control; put an 'Update' button on `storeagain`. Lock finished presets so a stray store cannot overwrite them.

capability: Presets leave playing media alone unless told to restart it
what_it_does: A Scene stores everything and so tends to restart media when recalled; the manual warns about this and steers operators to Cues, which store only chosen parameters. The FAQ's fix for audio that restarts on a cue is to untick the player's Replay value inside that cue.
max_check: Read pattrstorage's refpage: 'active <client> 0' leaves a client out of every recall; 'subscribemode' with 'subscribe' makes the object manage only a listed set of clients; 'priority' sets the order clients are restored in.
advice: Decide which controls are state and which are actions. Leave play, restart and file-load controls out of pattrstorage (`active <name> 0`, or `@subscribemode 1` with an explicit list), or every preset recall will restart the clips. Use one pattrstorage per concern (looks, media, mix) the way MadMapper uses one row per concern.

capability: A project is a folder, and one command collects every outside file into it
what_it_does: A project is a folder holding the project files, auto-saves and a resources folder. Collect External Resources copies every referenced movie, sound and image into it, so the folder can be moved to the show computer or archived whole.
max_check: Read the userguide topic projects: a Max Project collects patchers, media, code and externals, is saved automatically, and puts its own files ahead of the global search path. Manage Project offers Consolidate (copy all dependencies into the project folder) and Archive (one .maxzip file). Whether a media file named only inside a message box counts as a dependency was not checked.
advice: For anything that will run on another machine, save it as a Project and Consolidate before moving it. Keep media in the project folder and load it by file name, not by an absolute path, so the copy still finds it.

capability: Settings are split in two: this computer, and this project
what_it_does: Preferences have two tabs. Application holds what belongs to the machine: audio device, capture devices, graphics options. Project holds what belongs to the piece and travels with it: MIDI devices, OSC ports, DMX routing, engine frame rate, whether to open fullscreen.
max_check: Read the userguide topic OSC: the UDP server is switched on either for the whole application in the preferences or for one patcher in the patcher inspector. The video_engine topic: the video engine is an application preference that an object can override with @engine. The mapping topic: mappings belong to a patcher. So Max has both levels, but a patch's own machine choices (which display, which port, which camera) have no set home.
advice: Keep machine-specific choices out of the piece's presets. Put display index, audio device, MIDI port names and camera names in one small config file (a `dict` read at load) so that moving to another computer means editing one file, and the presets stay about the piece.

capability: Saving during a show is treated as a risk: a countdown, a pause button, and rotating backups
what_it_does: AutoSave writes recovery files, never over the project itself, and shows a ten-second countdown first so a performer can cancel it; the manual gives a drop in frame rate during the save as one reason. A toolbar button pauses it until quit. Each manual save keeps the previous version, up to a set number.
max_check: Read pattrstorage's refpage: 'savemode' chooses between prompting and saving the preset file automatically when the patcher is saved or freed; 'backupmode' keeps a set number of rotating backup files. The userguide says projects are saved automatically, and a page on messages to Max mentions crash recovery as a Max preference.
advice: Set `@backupmode` on pattrstorage so a bad store during rehearsal can be undone from the previous file. Do not write files while performing: trigger preset saves from an explicit button used between pieces, not from a timer.

capability: Sources that are not on screen stop working unless marked 'keep running'
what_it_does: A network video source is only processed while a visible surface uses it; a tick box keeps it running in the background for instant availability, and is labelled as costing more. The media preview and the two editing views can be switched off to save rendering.
max_check: Read the refpages: jit.movie has 'start' and 'stop'; jit.grab has 'open' and 'close'; the shared jit.gl attribute 'enable' turns an object's drawing off; the jit.fx objects have 'enable' and 'bypass'. Nothing stops a source by itself when its layer becomes invisible.
advice: When a layer's opacity reaches 0, also stop what feeds it: `stop` the movie, `enable 0` on its effects. Where an instant return matters more than the cost, leave it running and say so in a comment. Give every preview a toggle; a preview is a second render.

capability: Hover help: a status line explains whatever is under the mouse
what_it_does: A line at the bottom of the window describes the control the mouse is over, for every control in the program.
max_check: Read the userguide topic objects, section Annotations and Hints: @annotation sets the text the Clue bar shows when hovering over an object, and @hint adds a pop-up that appears only when the patcher is locked.
advice: Give every presentation control a `hint`. It costs one attribute per control and is the only documentation an operator sees in the middle of a show.

capability: An LFO is a ready-made module: shape, free or tempo-synced, speed, phase, range, and a bank of ten with spread
what_it_does: An Oscillator module outputs a value between 0 and 1 with a chosen wave shape, running at a set speed or locked to the tempo, with phase and range. The 2D version gives two related values; the Bank gives ten whose phases are spread by one Offset control. Any parameter can take one as its control.
max_check: Read jit.mo.time's refpage (bundled jit.mo package): in 'mode function' it outputs line, sin, saw or perlin values in step with the render context, with 'freq', 'phase', 'speed', 'scale', 'offset', and an 'interval' in Max time format so it can be tempo-relative. Read jit.mo.func's refpage: the same functions spread across the cells of a matrix, with 'freq' and 'phase', which gives many phase-offset values at once.
advice: For values that drive visuals, use jit.mo.time @mode function; it ticks with the render, so there is no metro to keep in step. Its `interval` takes Max time values, so a note value locks it to the transport's tempo. For a spread of related values, read them from one jit.mo.func matrix.

capability: Mixing two control sources on one parameter is done by a module that says how
what_it_does: A parameter takes one Control per kind of source. To let several inputs act on it, a Controls Combiner module mixes them using a chosen combination mode. A Macro module does the reverse: one widget that many Controls point at.
max_check: Read maximum's refpage: outputs the greater of the incoming value and its stored one. In Max several message cords into one inlet do not combine: each message simply replaces the last (the repo's CLAUDE.md notes that only signal cords sum). So Max allows any number of sources, which MadMapper does not, but states no rule for how they meet.
advice: When two things drive one parameter, an LFO and a fader, audio and a preset, put the rule in the patch as a visible object: `maximum`, `*` or `+`. Two cords into one inlet is 'last one wins', and it looks deliberate when it is not.
notes: The combination modes the Controls Combiner offers are not listed in the documents read.
theme: Effect chains: blend, amount and mask on each stage

capability: Two clips kept frame-locked by putting them side by side in one file
what_it_does: The documented way to keep two videos in step is to make one wide file with both side by side, then let two surfaces each crop their half. One decoder cannot drift from itself.
max_check: Read jit.fx.subtexture's refpage: a sub-region of a texture by 'offset' and 'dim', without copying. jit.movie's refpage offers 'time' and 'frame' for seeking but nothing that slaves one movie to another.
advice: For clips that must stay in step, including one picture split across projectors, play one wide movie and cut it with jit.fx.subtexture. Do not start two jit.movie objects together and hope.
notes: Not tested in Max; the reasoning is MadMapper's, applied to Max objects whose refpages were read.

capability: Game controllers arrive with named buttons, sticks and triggers
what_it_does: PlayStation and Xbox controllers and generic USB HID devices are control sources. Their inputs are offered by name, and each mapping has the same range, filter, curve and toggle settings as any other Control.
max_check: Read gamepad's refpage: reports button, joystick, trigger and sensor events from all connected controllers through the SDL library's mapped names, can load extra controller mappings, and sends rumble and LED colour back with 'senddevice'. The registry digest for hi calls it legacy.
advice: Use `gamepad`, not `hi`, for controllers: the inputs come out already named, and it can drive rumble and the light bar, which MadMapper's page does not offer.
notes: Max is at least level here.

capability: Comparisons that report the moment they change, not only their state
what_it_does: Each comparison actor has three outputs: the 1 or 0 result, a trigger when the result turns true, and a trigger when it turns false. A 'notify' input chooses between sending the result on every input or only when it changes. Inside Range does the same for a low/high range, with 'enter' and 'exit' triggers.
max_check: Read refpages. `>` and `==` output 1 or 0 for every number received in the left inlet; neither has a change-only mode or an edge outlet. `change` passes a number only if it differs from the stored one. `togedge` bangs its left outlet on a 0-to-1 transition and its right outlet on 1-to-0. `split` sends in-range numbers left and the rest right, with no enter or exit event.
advice: In Max a comparison that drives an event needs two more boxes: put `togedge` (or `change` then `select 1 0`) straight under the `>`, or the event re-fires on every incoming number. For a range, feed `split`'s two outlets into `1` and `0` messages, then `togedge`.
notes: One Isadora actor does the work of three Max objects. The missing `change` is a common cause of events that fire continuously in Max.

capability: Threshold with a dead band built in
what_it_does: A threshold with separate low and high values. The output turns on above the high value and off below the low value, and nothing happens in between, so a noisy value sitting near one threshold does not chatter. It also sends a trigger for each crossing.
max_check: Searched obj-qlookup.json for 'hyst' and 'schmitt': no core object. Read `past`: one threshold, bangs when a number rises above it, and re-arms only after a lower number or a `clear`. `thresh~` is the signal-rate version (digest only read). The package library lists `dot.schmitt` (high and low thresholds, one trigger outlet), `mo.schmitt` and `dk.schmitt`.
advice: Never put a bare `>` or `past` on sensor data. Use `dot.schmitt` or `mo.schmitt` when the package is installed; otherwise write the two-threshold latch in a few lines of `v8`. A core-only abstraction for this is worth having.

capability: Named actors for 'nothing happened', 'too many at once' and 'all together'
what_it_does: Trigger Delay restarts its wait on every new trigger, so it fires only after triggers stop arriving. Multi Blocker passes the first value and drops any that follow within a set time. Simultaneity fires once when all of its trigger inputs have fired inside a time window.
max_check: Read refpages. `delay` holds a bang for a time and has `stop`; its refpage does not say what a second bang does while one is pending, and its help file has no comment on it either. `speedlim` passes a message only after a minimum time since the last one, with a `usurp` option to keep the newest. `buddy` waits until every inlet has received something, with no time limit. `thresh` and `quickthresh` collect numbers that arrive close together into one list.
advice: The nearest thing to Multi Blocker is `speedlim`; check in the patch whether a held message is dropped or sent late, since Multi Blocker drops. For 'all inputs within N ms' Max has no single object: `buddy` never times out, so add a `delay` that sends it `clear`, or do it in `v8`. For 'no input for N ms', test what `delay` does on a second bang in the patch itself before relying on it, since the refpage is silent.
notes: The `delay` re-trigger behaviour is the one thing here not confirmed from Max's own docs.

capability: Clock that pauses in place and deals its ticks round-robin
what_it_does: Pulse Generator fires at a frequency in Hz. Turning 'run/stop' off pauses it and turning it on continues from where it was in the cycle; 'reset' starts the cycle again. With several outputs it fires them in turn. Sequential Trigger and Trigger Divider do the round-robin and the divide-by-N on any trigger stream.
max_check: Read refpages. `metro` takes an interval in milliseconds or a note value, starts with a bang or non-zero number and stops with 0 or `stop`; there is an `active` attribute but no pause that keeps the position inside the interval. `cycle` sends each bang or number to the next outlet in turn, with `set` to choose the next outlet. `counter` counts bangs within a range.
advice: Round-robin triggers are `metro` into `cycle N`; a divider is `counter` into `select`. Note that Max thinks in milliseconds per tick and Isadora in ticks per second. If a pulse must resume mid-interval after a pause, Max needs a `v8` or signal-rate clock; `metro` always starts a fresh interval.

capability: Control-rate LFO as one object
what_it_does: Outputs a continuously changing number following a sine, square, triangle, sawtooth or stepped-random wave, at 0.0001 to 999 Hz. It has a phase offset, a reset trigger, and a 'once' mode that runs a single cycle per reset.
max_check: Searched obj-qlookup.json for 'lfo': no core object. The package library lists `mo.lfo~` (signal and data outlets), `vs_lfo` (texture and data, needs Vsynth's renderer) and `Abl.LFO~`. The core route is a signal oscillator sampled down to messages, which needs audio running; that part is from the repo's patching notes, not a refpage read this session.
advice: A message-rate LFO with shape, phase, reset and one-shot is worth building as a small `v8` object, so video and lighting patches do not need DSP switched on to animate a number.

capability: Multi-segment envelope that can advance one segment per trigger
what_it_does: A ramp of up to nine segments (99 in the ++ version), each with a time and a target value. A trigger mode chooses between running the whole envelope per trigger and running one segment per trigger, with an end trigger either per segment or at the end.
max_check: Read refpages. `line` takes a list of target-time pairs and has `pause`, `resume` and `stop`. `function` is a drawn breakpoint editor that outputs a list for `line`; breakpoints can be marked as sustain points, a bang plays up to the first sustain point and `next` continues from it. `bline` advances a ramp one step per bang.
advice: The Max match for 'one segment per trigger' is `function` with sustain points: bang to start, `next` on each later cue. The envelope is then drawn, not typed into eighteen inputs, which is the better editing surface. Use it for cue-stepped fades.

capability: Eased ramp with a speed limit, pause and a 'done' trigger
what_it_does: Ramps from a start to an end value over a duration along an s-curve whose steepness is one input. A 'max delta' input caps the rate of change, stretching the ramp when needed. It sends a trigger on completion; the 2D version ramps a point, with pause, resume and a 'moving' flag. Curvature bends any value along a two-control-point curve drawn on the actor.
max_check: Read `line` (linear ramps, pause and resume) and the installed ease package's `ease.maxref.xml`: `ease` applies a chosen easing function to an incoming float, with `input_range` and `output_range` attributes. It shapes a value; it does not generate the ramp. `function` has per-segment curve values (`setcurve`, `xyc`).
advice: Keep the two jobs apart in Max: `line` makes a linear 0-to-1 ramp, `ease` shapes it. That is more flexible than Isadora's single actor. What Max lacks is the rate cap: work out the time as distance divided by maximum speed before sending the pair to `line`.
notes: `ease` is a third-party package on this machine, not part of Max.

capability: Move toward a target at a fixed rate
what_it_does: The output moves continuously toward whatever target value it is given, at a set amount per second, and stops when it gets there. A new target simply changes where it is heading.
max_check: Searched obj-qlookup.json for 'slew': nothing at message rate. Read `slide`: it filters each incoming value by a formula applied per input, so it moves only when a value or a bang arrives and its speed depends on how often that happens. `line` reaches a target in a given time, not at a given rate.
advice: For constant-speed motion in Max, read the current value, compute time = distance / rate, and send target and time to `line`. Do not use `slide` for anything that must take a known time. A small 'seek' abstraction around `line` is worth keeping.

capability: Smoothing and decay that run on their own clock
what_it_does: Smoother filters a noisy number with one 0-to-1 smoothing amount and outputs at its own frequency, whether or not new input arrives. Decay Generator is a level that jumps up by a set amount on each trigger and falls at a set amount per second, giving a measure of how busy a trigger stream is.
max_check: Read `slide`: separate slide-up and slide-down values, and a bang 'performs the same function as float using the last input value'. It produces output only when it receives something. The package library lists `mo.smooth` (leaky integrator with up and down times in ms) and `dot.aggregate.leaky` (integrator with a leak).
advice: In Max, drive `slide` from a `metro` so it keeps settling after the sensor goes quiet; without the clock it freezes part-way. For an activity meter use `dot.aggregate.leaky`, or `accum` plus a clocked subtraction.

capability: Counter with a step size, limit-or-wrap, floats, and a settable current value
what_it_does: Adds or subtracts a set amount on its 'add' and 'sub' triggers, between a minimum and maximum. A mode chooses between stopping at the ends and wrapping. The current value is itself an input, so it can be preset or given a start value. Float Counter is the same with decimals.
max_check: Read refpages. `counter` counts whole numbers by one, up, down or up-and-down, between a minimum and maximum, with `set`, `jam`, `inc`, `dec` and carry outlets at the ends. `accum` stores a number and adds or multiplies into it, int or float, with no limits.
advice: Use `counter` for stepping through indexes; its up-and-down mode and carry outlets go beyond Isadora's. For a bounded float or a step other than one, use `accum` followed by `clip` or `%`, or `v8`. Do not force `counter` to do it.

capability: Toggle whose starting state is declared: on, off, or as last saved
what_it_does: A trigger-driven on/off switch with an 'init' input: 'on' or 'off' sends that state every time the Scene starts, and 'none' keeps whatever state was saved with the document.
max_check: Read refpages. `toggle` has no start-state attribute of its own; it has `parameter_enable` ('setting initial parameter values in Max'). `pattr` has `autorestore` (output the last-saved value at load) and `initial` (restore this value instead). `loadmess` sends a typed message at load.
advice: Decide for every stateful control in Max which of the three it is: always starts off (nothing needed), always starts at a value (`loadmess` through the control), or restores (`pattr` or parameter mode). Isadora makes the choice visible on the actor; in Max it is spread over three mechanisms, so say which one in a comment.

capability: Change filter with a minimum-change amount, that reports its value on start
what_it_does: Passes a value on only when it differs from the last output by at least a set amount, with a trigger alongside. When its Scene starts it sends the current input value once, so whatever follows begins in the right state.
max_check: Read `change`: passes a number only if different from the stored one; its modes report increase or decrease. There is no tolerance, so a float that jitters in its last digits passes every time. `round` rounds to a multiple of a given number.
advice: For noisy floats in Max, quantise before `change` (`round 0.01` then `change`), or write the dead band in `v8`. Also copy the second half: a filter that holds state should send it once at load, or the first real change is the first thing downstream ever sees.

capability: Running minimum and maximum, and self-calibrating ranges
what_it_does: Hold Range reports the lowest and highest value ever seen and the span between them. Calc Brightness has a measure trigger that watches a set number of frames and then rescales its output to the range it saw. Limit-Scale Value clips an input to one range and then maps it to another.
max_check: Read refpages. `peak` outputs a number when it exceeds the stored peak; `trough` does the opposite, and its stored value starts at 128. `scale` maps one range to another and its refpage says inputs 'are not clipped to this range'. `zmap` clips to its ranges but 'does not allow inverted scaling'.
advice: The Max calibration pattern is `peak` and `trough` feeding the input-range inlets of `scale`. Two traps: `trough` starts at 128, so send it a large value first, and `scale` overshoots outside its input range, so follow it with `clip` or use `zmap` when no inversion is needed.

capability: Selector that re-sends the chosen input's current value when the choice changes
what_it_does: Selector routes one of several inputs to one output. When the selection changes it immediately sends the current value of the newly chosen input, so the output is never stale. The inputs are typed by the first link made, and can carry video.
max_check: Read refpages. `switch`: a number in the left inlet 'specifies an open inlet for receiving subsequent messages'. It holds no values, so changing the selection outputs nothing until the newly opened inlet receives a message. `gate` is the same in the other direction.
advice: After changing a `switch` in Max, the output still shows the old source until the new one speaks. Where that matters, keep each source's latest value in an `int`, `float` or `pv` and bang the chosen one when the selection changes, or do the selection in `v8`.
notes: A frequent cause of 'the menu changed but nothing happened' in Max patches.
theme: Names and scope: send, receive, variables

capability: Routing and bypass that stop the upstream work
what_it_does: Gate, Router and Selector have a hidden 'exec src' input. Set to 'gated', every actor upstream of a closed path stops executing, and the links turn red to show it. Separately, nearly every video effect has a 'bypass' input, Projector has 'active', and Movie Player has 'visible', which unloads the movie when off.
max_check: Read refpages. Max objects send messages onward when they receive them, so a closed `gate` below a chain does not stop the chain computing. `jit.gl.slab` has `bypass` ('the input is passed through to the output without processing'); `jit.gl.pix` lists `bypass` with no description. The GL group page gives every GL object `enable` ('drawing is enabled'). The matrix-operator group page lists no bypass attribute.
advice: In Max, close the path at the top: put the `gate` above the expensive chain, or stop the `metro` that drives it. A gate at the bottom saves nothing. Use `@bypass` on slabs and `@enable 0` on GL objects, and expose both where the operator can see them.

capability: Switching a whole sub-patch off from inside it
what_it_does: An actor placed inside a User Actor or Macro, with one 'enable' input. Off, every actor inside stops executing. Wired to a User Input, it gives the sub-patch an on/off input of its own.
max_check: Read refpages. `pcontrol`: 'the word enable followed by a 1 or a 0 will turn MIDI and Audio' on or off in connected subpatchers. `mute~` disables only the signal objects in a subpatcher. `poly~`'s `mute` turns off signal processing for one instance. None of them stops ordinary messages, timers or Jitter objects inside a `p` or abstraction.
advice: Give every heavy Max abstraction an enable inlet that gates its own clocks and inputs at the top, and sets `@enable` on its GL objects. For audio, load it in `poly~` and mute the instance. There is no one-box equivalent, so make it a convention.
theme: Encapsulation: ports, arguments, on and off

capability: Sub-patch ports declared with a name, type, range and help text
what_it_does: Each port of a sub-patch is an actor whose dialog sets the port's name, data type (integer, float, trigger, on/off, video, a media file number and others), its minimum and maximum, and the help text shown on hover. Port order is set in a reorder dialog, not by where the actors sit. The sub-patch itself has its own help text.
max_check: Read `inlet`: its attributes are `comment` (the hover text, 'can only be set using the Comment setting in the inlet object's Inspector'), `cool` and a colour. No type or range. The userguide's subpatchers page says inlet order follows the position of the inlet objects, so moving one re-wires the parent.
advice: Max gives a port only a hover comment, so put the type and range in it ('float 0.-1.: mix') and clamp inside with `clip`. Keep inlets in a strict left-to-right row and never nudge one sideways past another. This is the repo's labelling rule; Isadora shows what it is standing in for.

capability: Wireless sends on numbered, typed channels that also carry video
what_it_does: Broadcaster sends any value, including a video stream, on a channel number. Every Listener on that number in any active Scene receives it. A Listener declares the type it outputs and converts to it, and has a trigger output beside its value. Their main documented use is passing values between Scenes that run at the same time.
max_check: Read `send` and `receive`: names, not numbers; any message; reaches every `receive` of the same name in every open patcher window. The repo's patching notes quote the refpage that the order two receivers fire in is not deterministic.
advice: Max's names are easier to read than channel numbers; keep them descriptive. The scoping differs: Isadora limits a broadcast to active Scenes, while Max's `s`/`r` reach every open patch, so anything loaded twice needs `#0` or `---` in the name.
theme: Names and scope: send, receive, variables

capability: Named sets of global values that announce their own changes
what_it_does: A named collection of values that outlives Scene changes. Set writes the collection; any active Get with the same name outputs all the values whenever a Set is triggered, and also when its own Scene starts. Streams such as video are refused, and a trigger cannot be stored.
max_check: Read refpages. `value`: objects with the same name share one stored message, and 'you can get the contents out of a particular value object by sending it a bang', so readers are not told when it changes. `pv` is the same, limited to one patcher and its subpatchers. `dict` is a named store with keys.
advice: In Max a shared `value` is passive: pair it with an `s`/`r` of the same name when other parts of the patch must react to a change. For a named group of settings use one `dict`, not many `value` objects.

capability: A start value on any input, applied on activation and pushed through the patch
what_it_does: Any input can be given an 'Init' value that it takes each time its Scene starts. Since version 2 that value also makes the actor execute, so results travel downstream. Without Init, an input keeps the value it had when the Scene was left. Enter Scene Value and Enter Scene Trigger are the patched alternative.
source_urls: https://troikatronix.com/files/isadora-manual.pdf#page=483 (Actors Reference: Enter Scene Trigger / Enter Scene Value)
max_check: Read `loadmess` (sends its typed message at load, with a `defer` option), `loadbang`, and `pattr` (`autorestore`, `initial`). The userguide's patcher_lifecycle page says a patcher is initialised in phases, with objects created before any loadbang or loadmess fires, and subpatchers firing before their parents.
advice: A Max creation argument is Isadora's old behaviour: it sets the object silently and nothing downstream hears about it. When later objects or displays must start in agreement, send the value through the control with `loadmess`. When they need not, the argument alone is enough and an extra `loadmess` is clutter.
notes: The Isadora author's own account of why silent initial values caused trouble is in the KB article.

capability: Evaluation by pulling from the end of each chain, top-to-bottom for ties
what_it_does: Isadora works in cycles. Each cycle it starts from actors at the end of a chain and executes whatever is upstream of each input. When several links feed one input, the upstream actors run from top to bottom of the screen and the last one to produce a value wins. Every input holds its latest value, and a trigger input fires when any new value reaches it.
max_check: The repo's `patching/MAX_PATCHING.md` (promoted from Max's userguide) says Max walks the graph depth-first within one event and that `trigger` fires right to left; the repo's `CLAUDE.md` quotes `trigger`'s refpage for the same order. Neither page was re-opened this session. Max pushes each message as it happens; there is no per-cycle pass and no stored value on a cold inlet until something sets it.
advice: Do not carry Isadora habits into Max: position on screen is not a safe way to order things, several cords into one inlet arrive as separate events, and an inlet has no value until it receives one. Make order explicit with `trigger`, and convert values to bangs explicitly with `t b`.
notes: The KB article describes version 2; the v4 manual does not restate the algorithm.

capability: Table actor with read-on-start and write-on-exit file modes
what_it_does: A list of lines, each with a set number of numeric or text items, with one input and one output per item. Lines are added, inserted, replaced, deleted and recalled by number. A tab-separated text file can back it, with a mode that reads on activation, writes on deactivation, both or neither, and a switch for keeping a copy inside the document.
max_check: Read refpages. `coll`: when a patch with a named coll loads, Max looks for a file of that name and loads it; `embed` saves the data in the patcher; `write` and `writeagain` save on request. `dict` takes a file name as an argument to import on load and has `embed`. `closebang` sends a bang when its patcher window closes. Nothing writes back by itself.
advice: In Max say where the data lives: `@embed 1` for data that belongs to the patch, a named file for data that outlives it. For write-on-exit, wire `closebang` to `writeagain`. `coll` returns a whole line as a list, so follow it with `unjoin` to get Isadora's one-outlet-per-column.

capability: Text as its own value type, with small actors for cutting and joining
what_it_does: Text is a link type. Small actors take the first, last or middle characters or lines, append to a growing string, wrap at a line length, compare two strings with or without case, and build formatted text from up to nine parameters.
max_check: obj-qlookup.json lists about forty `string.*` objects in Max 9 (append, compare, contains, indexof, length, replace, slice, split, sprintf, substring, tolower, trim and others). `string`'s refpage calls a string 'a block of text in memory that is not stored in Max's symbol table', and the userguide's strings page says the purpose-built String objects are easier and more efficient for text work than symbols. Also read the digests of `string.sprintf`, `string.split` and `string.substring`.
advice: In Max 9, treat text that changes while the patch runs as a `string`, not a symbol, and reach for `string.*` before `sprintf` and `regexp` chains. Max is now at least level with Isadora here, but only if the new family is used.
notes: Only four of the string objects' pages were opened; the rest are known by registry name.

capability: Keyboard watcher with a key range, key names and press/release choice
what_it_does: Keyboard Watcher is set to a key or a range of keys, written in quotes, with names for special keys such as 'right-arrow', and to press, release or both. Key Table Watcher holds up to 32 keys and outputs the position of the one pressed, which turns a row of keys into a selector.
max_check: Read `key` and `keyup`: no inlets and no filter; four outlets give the ASCII code, a platform-specific key code, the modifier keys and a platform-independent key code. The userguide's mapping page describes Max 9 Mappings, which bind key presses or MIDI to parameter-enabled objects with no patching.
advice: In Max filter keys with `select` under `key`, and take the fourth outlet when the patch must behave the same on Mac and Windows. For operator shortcuts, prefer Max 9 Mappings: the binding is then visible and editable outside the patch, which is what Isadora's Go Triggers give.

capability: Mouse position as a percentage of a region, gated by modifier keys
what_it_does: Reports the mouse as 0 to 100 percent across a chosen part of the display, only while a chosen set of modifier keys is held, with a trigger on each move. The Stage version does the same inside one output window and adds click triggers, an inside/outside flag and scroll-wheel values.
max_check: Read refpages. `mousestate` reports position in pixels plus deltas, buttons and wheel, on a bang or after `poll`, with a `mode` message for the coordinate reference; its description limits it to when the cursor is in a Max patcher window. `modifiers` reports modifier keys on a bang or at a polling rate. `jit.window` and `jit.world` report mouse events on their window from the dump outlet; `jit.window` has `idlemouse` to include movement without a button.
advice: For interaction on the video output in Max, take the mouse messages from the `jit.world` dump outlet, not from `mousestate`, and divide by the window size so the patch survives a change of resolution. Gate with `modifiers` and a `gate`.

capability: MIDI input actors with a range filter on every field
what_it_does: Each MIDI watcher takes a single value or a range for port, channel, and the message's own fields (pitch and velocity, or controller and value). A message must fall inside all of them to be seen. The outputs give the matched values and a trigger.
max_check: Read `notein`: arguments choose a port or device and a channel; outlets are pitch, velocity and channel, with no range filter. `stripnote` passes only note-ons. `split` passes a number range. `midiselect` separates a raw MIDI stream by attribute.
advice: In Max the filter is patched after the input: `notein` to `stripnote` to `split`. That is one more box per condition, but each condition is visible on the patch, and a `kslider` or `live.dial` can sit in the path to show what arrived.

capability: Note sender that owns its note-offs
what_it_does: Send Note sends a note-on per trigger and, if a duration is set, the matching note-off later; a 'quiet' switch silences the previous note first. All Notes Off sends note-offs only for notes Isadora knows are sounding. Mini Sequencer plays one of a list of pitches per selection and silences the last one on leaving the Scene.
max_check: Read refpages. `makenote` pairs a pitch with a velocity and sends the note-off after a duration; `stop` sends note-offs for everything it holds, `clear` forgets them, and `repeatmode` sets what a repeated pitch does. `flush` and `midiflush` track note-ons passing through and send the missing note-offs on a bang.
advice: Same idea in both tools. In Max route every generated note through `makenote`, or put `flush` before `noteout`, and send `stop` or a bang whenever the transport or the section stops. Isadora does this on leaving a Scene; Max will leave notes hanging unless it is wired.

capability: OSC listener with wildcards, a backlog counter and a choice about dropping
what_it_does: OSC Address Listener matches an address pattern with * wildcards and outputs the values, the matched address and a JSON copy of the message. A 'one per cycle' switch chooses between always showing the newest message, dropping any that arrive faster than the patch runs, and queueing every message, with a 'pending msgs' output showing the backlog.
max_check: Read refpages. `udpreceive` has one data outlet, a `maxqueuesize` message, `defer` and `outputformat`. `osc.packet` stores an OSC packet and converts formats. `param.osc` maps OSC onto a patch's parameters. The package library lists `o.route` as the current address router and marks CNMAT's `osc-route` deprecated. `qlim` and `speedlim` limit message rate.
advice: Max makes no drop-or-queue decision visible. On any high-rate OSC stream, decide it yourself: `speedlim` or `qlim` after `udpreceive` for 'newest wins', and know that `maxqueuesize` exists. Use `o.route` for address patterns.
notes: What `udpreceive` does when its queue is full was not read.

capability: Movie play segment as start plus length, with position measured inside it
what_it_does: The part of a movie that plays is set by 'play start' and 'play length', both as a percentage of the file. The 'position' input jumps within that segment. Loop is off, on or palindrome. Outputs give a trigger per new frame, a trigger at each loop end and the position. Helper actors convert between seconds and percent for a given file.
max_check: Read refpages. `jit.movie`: `looppoints` in the movie's time units, plus `looppoints_ms` and `looppoints_secs`; `position` is normalised 0 to 1 over the whole movie; `loopreport` sends `loopnotify` at the loop point (both ends in palindrome); `unique` outputs only new frames; `rate` sets speed. `jit.playlist`: `selection <clip> <start> <end>` in a normalised range, `selectionms`, `loopreport`, `reportprogress`.
advice: In Max state loop points in seconds (`looppoints_secs`) or use `jit.playlist`'s `selection`, and turn on `@loopreport 1` and `@unique 1` to get Isadora's loop-end and new-frame triggers. Max's `position` covers the whole file, not the loop, so rescale it when scrubbing inside a loop.

capability: Codec advice tied to how the clip will be played
what_it_does: The documentation gives one rule: clips that are scrubbed, reversed, sped up or looped tightly should use a codec that stores every frame whole (HAP, ProRes, Photo JPEG), and H.264 is only for playing straight through at normal speed. It also asks for one codec, one resolution and one frame rate per project, with the target frame rate matched to the display's refresh rate.
max_check: Listed Max's bundled packages: `hap` and `VIDDLL` are among them. Read `jit.movie`: the `engine` attribute chooses the video backend (avf, qt or viddll) and can only be set in the box. Max's own codec guidance was not read this session.
advice: The rule is about codecs, not Isadora, so apply it in Max too: before debugging stutter in a `jit.movie` that scrubs or runs backwards, check the file's codec. Keep one codec and one frame rate per piece.

capability: A premultiplied-alpha flag that travels with the video stream
what_it_does: Every video stream with an alpha channel carries a flag saying whether its colour is already multiplied by its alpha. Movie Player sets it per movie, and Alpha Tool can flip the flag or actually convert the image. The manual's symptom to look for is a light or dark halo on soft edges.
max_check: Searched every Max refpage for 'premult': no hits. The GL group page documents `blend` as named modes over `blend_mode` source and destination factors, where `alphablend` is `6 7` (source alpha, one minus source alpha) and factor 1 is 'one'.
advice: Max leaves this to the patcher. Dark fringes on soft edges usually mean a premultiplied source drawn with `alphablend`; try `@blend_mode 1 7` on that layer. Note in a comment which kind each source is, because nothing in Max carries the information.
notes: The `1 7` setting is worked out from the factor table in the refpage; it was not tested in Max.

capability: Output layer with three blend choices and one 'intensity' input
what_it_does: Projector draws a stream on a Stage with a 'layer' number and a 'blend' of additive, transparent or opaque. One 'intensity' input means brightness under additive and opaque, and opacity under transparent, so a fade is always the same input. The manual warns that a transparent image must be on a higher layer than what it sits over.
max_check: Read the GL group refpage and Max's transform-defaults registry. `layer`: 'the layer number determines the rendering order (low to high). Objects in the same layer have no guarantee which will be rendered first.' `blend` has eight named modes (add, multiply, screen, exclusion, colorblend, alphablend, coloradd, alphaadd). `jit.gl.layer` loads with blending on and depth testing off; `jit.gl.videoplane` with blending off and depth on.
advice: Max offers more blend modes but no single fade input. Use `jit.gl.layer`, give every one an explicit `@layer`, since equal layers draw in no fixed order, and fade with the alpha of `color` under `alphablend` or by scaling `color`'s red, green and blue under `add`.
theme: Draw order and layering stated outright

capability: Keyers and masks that can output transparency instead of a finished mix
what_it_does: The two keyers normally output foreground mixed over background. With their 'alpha' switch on they output the foreground with a transparent hole, for the Projector to composite over whatever is on lower layers. Add Alpha Channel attaches any stream as another stream's alpha. Alpha Mask mixes two streams by a third and has a 'strength' input for fading the mask in.
max_check: Read refpages. `jit.chromakey` and `jit.lumakey` take `tol` and `fade` and have a `mode`: 0 performs the key and outputs the mix, 1 outputs the key map 'for use elsewhere'. `jit.alphablend` crossfades two matrices by the alpha plane of the left one. These are CPU matrix objects.
advice: In Max, prefer keying to alpha and letting `jit.gl.layer` do the mix: take the key map (`@mode 1`), use it as the alpha of the foreground, and layer it. That keeps the background free to be anything on a lower layer, which is the design Isadora's 'alpha' switch points at.
theme: Draw order and layering stated outright

capability: A stated rule for mixing streams of different sizes
what_it_does: When two streams of different resolution meet, one is scaled to match. A preference sets the default rule, and Video Mixer's 'frame scale' input can override it per actor: largest, smallest, or the minimum or maximum width or height. The manual tells users to keep every stream the same size because the scaling costs time.
max_check: Read refpages. `jit.gl.slab` and `jit.gl.pix`: `adapt` (default 1) makes the output size match the input; with it off, `dim` sets the size, and `dimscale` multiplies it. `jit.xfade`'s own page lists only the crossfade amount; the matrix-operator group page gives every such object `adapt`.
advice: In Max the output size of a two-input slab follows an input unless told otherwise. Where sources differ, set `@adapt 0 @dim <w> <h>` on the mixing object so the size is a decision written on the box, and keep every source at that size upstream.
notes: Which input `adapt` follows on a multi-input slab was not read.
theme: Effect chains: blend, amount and mask on each stage

capability: Frame bank and video delay as single actors
what_it_does: Buffer stores a set number of frames in turn and outputs whichever one its 'select' input names, with a mode that stops when full and a trigger when the last frame is stored. Video Delay is a chain of frames of a set length. Freeze holds a frame while a switch is on, or grabs one on a trigger.
max_check: Read `jit.matrixset`: a set of `matrixcount` matrices; `index` chooses which one an incoming matrix is written to; `thru` passes input on; it can import and export movies.
